andytown llc.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to a beneficial ownership certification, KYC on Lauren Crabbe and Michael McCrory with the adverse media articles cleared against his identifiers, and a debt schedule covering the 2025 United Business Bank and SBA facilities.

body.text: ANDYTOWN LLC is a Delaware LLC (file 6308018, registered 7 February 2017) that converted out of its original California domestic filing (201303910168, registered 19 December 2012), which is why that filing reads inactive. It is qualified in California as a foreign LLC (201707510557, registered 7 March 2017), active and in good standing; that filing carries the submitted name and the submitted office address, 3016 Taraval St, San Francisco.

San Francisco business registrations list two trade names owned by Andytown LLC, Andytown Coffee Roasters and Private Events. The website, which was not submitted, presents the business as Andytown Coffee Roasters rather than the legal name.

gaps.point: Whether the Delaware LLC is in good standing: Delaware publishes no filing status.
gaps.noAction: Delaware publishes no status; the California foreign qualification, where the business operates, is active and in good standing.

body.text: The watchlist screen returned one entry, MICHAEL COX on the BIS Denied Persons List, against the manager Michael McCrory. The name differs and the screen classes it as a close match, not a valid hit; no other list returned a result for the business or its people.
The PEP screen found no hits on the submitted individuals or their relatives and close associates.

The adverse media screen returned 18 negative articles matched by name to Michael McCrory: coverage of an Ontario classic-car theft and fraud prosecution (Petrolia Lambton Independent, 2025), reports of a drowning in Anderson, Indiana and a traffic crash in Kansas, and a Barnes & Thornburg retirement-plan settlement. No article is matched to the business, and nothing on the record ties any of them to this Michael McCrory beyond the name.

gaps.point: Whether any of the adverse media articles concerns the submitted Michael McCrory or a namesake.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A reviewer disposition of each article against Michael McCrory's KYC identifiers (date of birth, residential address).

gaps.point: Criminal history of Lauren Crabbe and Michael McCrory.
gaps.noAction: Not ordered and not a standard requirement for opening a business deposit account; its absence carries no weight.

body.text: The business classifies as a snack and nonalcoholic beverage bar (NAICS 722515; MCC 5814), with coffee and tea manufacturing as a secondary classification, outside high-risk and prohibited categories. Its website, andytownsf.com, is online as a Shopify storefront selling coffee, consistent with that classification. No third-party profiles were found.

The submitted office address, 3016 Taraval St, San Francisco, is a deliverable commercial property; the website shows it and names the submitted person, and the business is active in California. San Francisco business registrations on the record place Andytown LLC at several city locations, including restaurant and mobile food facility registrations.

gaps.point: Whether each location holds a current San Francisco health permit.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A San Francisco Department of Public Health food permit lookup for each location.
gaps.noAction: Food-service permitting is ordinary for the line of work and is not a condition of opening a deposit account.

body.text: The California filings name Lauren Crabbe (chief executive officer, manager and California registered agent) and Michael McCrory (manager), both submitted, and the submitted person is matched to the filing. The Delaware filing names no members or managers, only its registered agent, Cogency Global Inc.; no business entity appears as an owner or officer.

Four connections were found, all through shared addresses and none through a shared person: Bio-People Unlimited at the 3016 Taraval St office, Occidental Power LLC at 3629 Taraval St, and Helen Lee Sushi Bar LLC and Gus's Community Market LLC at 2111 Harrison St, all commercial premises where the business trades.

gaps.point: Members, ownership percentages and any 25% beneficial owners of the Delaware LLC.
Identity verification of Lauren Crabbe and Michael McCrory.

body.text: Eight UCC filings are open. Two are equipment finance from Carbonic Service on an ice machine and a water machine (2022), with a further Navitas Credit Corp filing (2023); the SBA holds a 2020 lien on all assets, including deposit accounts, and a second filing from September 2025. United Business Bank filed in California and Delaware on 29 September 2025, the California filing a blanket lien on equipment, inventory, accounts and general intangibles, and T Corporation System filed as representative in 2023. Ten earlier filings, most by Bank of San Francisco in 2016 and 2017, are closed, and no tax lien is on record.

One litigation names the business: Chelette Dewees v. ANDYTOWN LLC, a civil rights action in San Mateo County Superior Court filed 31 October 2025 with the business as defendant, dismissed with prejudice on 23 June 2026 with no money judgment. There are no bankruptcy filings.

gaps.point: What the September 2025 United Business Bank and SBA filings secure, and whether those facilities are current: UCC filings state no amounts.
Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming Lauren Crabbe and Michael McCrory.
gaps.noAction: Not required to open a deposit account where the business-level record is established.

followUps.text:
Collect a beneficial ownership certification naming each member, their percentage and who holds control.
The Delaware filing names no members, and the California filings name only Lauren Crabbe and Michael McCrory as managers.

Run KYC on Lauren Crabbe and Michael McCrory.
Both are submitted and named on the filings; no identity verification is held.

Clear the 18 adverse media articles against Michael McCrory's KYC identifiers.
They are matched to his name only and cover an Ontario classic-car fraud case, accident reports and a law-firm settlement.

Request a debt schedule covering the United Business Bank and SBA facilities filed in September 2025.
The United Business Bank filing is a blanket lien and the SBA's 2020 lien reaches deposit accounts; the filings state no amounts.

firebird yarns.name: Bank account opening
firebird yarns.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to KYC on Kathryn Bernard, disposition of the adverse media match, and confirmation of whether the two Illinois collection suits name her.

body.text: FIREBIRD YARNS is a trade name of Kathryn Bernard, held on an active San Francisco business registration (account 1089962) at 1322 Haight St since 9 July 2018. The business is likely a sole proprietorship and has no Secretary of State filing in any state, which is the expected position for that form: there is no formation record and no good-standing status to obtain.
The website shows the submitted business name. No TIN was submitted.
The watchlist screen returned no hits across the OFAC, BIS and State Department lists, and the PEP screen returned no hits on Kathryn Bernard or her relatives and close associates.

Adverse media returned one name match to Kathryn Bernard (match score 0.87), made of two negative MSN Philippines items: one tagged fraud, bribery and corruption, the other narcotics and organised crime. The linked articles cover a U.S. Capitol riot panel's prosecution referrals and a record year of shootings in Sweden; neither is about the business, and nothing on the record ties either to her beyond the name.

gaps.point: Whether the two adverse media items concern the submitted Kathryn Bernard or a namesake.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A reviewer disposition of both articles against the owner's KYC identifiers.

gaps.point: Criminal history of Kathryn Bernard was not ordered.
gaps.noAction: Not standard for opening a deposit account; the watchlist and PEP screens are clear.

body.text: The business classifies as a sewing, needlework and piece goods store (MCC 5949), outside high-risk and prohibited categories. The website, firebirdyarns.com, is an online Shopify storefront on a domain registered in February 2018 that shows the submitted address; online Instagram, Facebook, Yelp and Google profiles list it as a yarn and craft store, the Google listing rated 4.6 across 106 reviews.

The submitted office address, 1322 Haight St, San Francisco, is verified, deliverable and commercial, consistent with a walk-in retail shop. The absence of a California state registration follows from the sole proprietorship form. The website does not name Kathryn Bernard.

gaps.point: Whether the shop holds a California seller's permit for its retail sales.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A CDTFA seller's permit lookup.
gaps.noAction: Yarn retail needs no professional licence, and a seller's permit is not a condition of opening a deposit account; the active San Francisco registration places the business at its address.

body.text: As a likely sole proprietorship, the business and its owner are one person: Kathryn Bernard, the submitted individual, named as owner on the San Francisco registration. There is no state filing to match her against, so the person check returns no match rather than a mismatch, and no beneficial ownership certification applies to the form.
No business connections were found; the structure is a single individual with no entity owners or registered agents.

gaps.point: Identity verification of Kathryn Bernard, the owner and signer.

body.text: UCC and tax lien searches found no liens, and there are no bankruptcy filings.

Two collection suits in Cook County Circuit Court, Illinois, name a Kathryn Bernard as defendant: TD Bank USA v. Bernard, Kathryn P (filed October 2022, status unknown, no judgment recorded) and Midland Credit v. Bernard Kathryn (filed October 2020), with a judgment for the plaintiff in January 2021 and a garnishment judgment in November 2022, amounts not stated. For a sole proprietorship the owner's personal obligations are the business's, but the suits are in Illinois and the shop has operated in San Francisco since 2018; nothing beyond the name ties them to her.

gaps.point: Whether the Cook County defendant is the submitted Kathryn Bernard, and if so whether the Midland judgment is satisfied.
Liens and bankruptcies naming Kathryn Bernard personally were not ordered.
gaps.noAction: The business-level lien and bankruptcy searches already cover the sole proprietor, and both are clear.

followUps.text:
Run KYC on Kathryn Bernard.
She is the sole proprietor and signer, and no identity verification is held.

Clear the adverse media match against her KYC identifiers.
Two negative MSN Philippines items tagged fraud, narcotics and organised crime match her name only.

Confirm whether the Cook County defendant is her and, if so, obtain the status of the TD Bank suit and evidence that the Midland judgment is satisfied.
As a sole proprietor, her personal judgments are the business's obligations.

recent_posts.text: New in the shop: Piedmont by Juniper Moon Farm! This sport weight yarn is 70% recycled cashmere / 30% recycled silk in 50 gram balls of 191yds / 175m.
Coming soon: new Fade Frenzy sets! Pulled from our stock of fingering weight hand dyed yarns, these collections of seven 25 gram mini skeins will be available in-store and on our website.

Tons of fresh house-dyed yarn is on the walls! We've got Sparkle DK, the return of 3-Ply Bulky, Sparkle Sock, and the brand new, ultra-luxe Yak Silk Sock.

✨️ Slide 1, Sparkle DK, L to R: 
Fanfic tropes: Mistaken Identity, Vampire AU, Fuck or Die, Huddling for Warmth, Fated Mates, Space Western, Miscommunication, Dream Talking, Enemies to Lovers, Wingfic

💪 Slide 2, 3-Ply Bulky, L to R: 
Petit Fours, Cardinal, Pumpkin Patch, Sundew, Fairy Princess, Velvet Couch, Pool Party, Crushed Grapes, Victoriana, Darkness

🦸‍♀️ Slide 3, Sparkle Sock, L to R: 
X-Men: Storm, Colossus, Deadpool, Juggernaut, Jubilee, Rogue, Iceman, Beast, Psylocke, Glob Herman

🐃 Slide 4, Yak Silk Sock (50g skeins), L to R:
Undyed, Velvet, Moss, Mystery, Spice, Kisses, Boudoir

An update on the new shop sample, the Lathyrus Cowl from Ksenia Naidyon 's new book One Skein Knitting. We're knitting the narrow version, the wide version has an additional repeat of the cable. It's working up beautifully in Sparkle DK yarn from Murky Depths Dyeworks in the colorway Persimmon.

A warm welcome to Armando, our 2026 pin-up! We had a lot of great name suggestions (15% of them were Hank 😂), but we had to honor his shapely biceps with a suitable name 💪 😉 

And congrats to our giveaway winner, yara 

Armando merch- totes, pins, and stickers- are available on our website and in our store.

Drool-worthy art by Stephen Draws 🕸️

On the rail, we've got a much-needed restock of 3-Ply Bulky, the ✨️new✨️ Yak Silk Sock, and everyone's fav, Irid Sparkle Sock. 
Which one is catching your eye?

We just received a restock of all your favorites from Amy Small 

#restock #lys #localyarnstore #handspun

Happy 8th Anniversary from us at Firebird Yarns! We've got a new pin-up, illustrated by Stephen Draws 🕸️ 

We're giving away a set of this year's pin-up merch: a tote bag, enamel pin, and sticker. The merch will be available for sale online and in-store as well, starting tomorrow afternoon, 9/1.

maverick games llc.name: Bank account opening
maverick games llc.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to confirming the line of work and any gaming licence it requires, dispositioning the OFAC SDN result, KYC on Christopher S Lochte, a beneficial ownership certification and a Certificate of Good Standing.

body.text: MAVERICK GAMES LLC holds one active domestic Arizona filing under the submitted name (file 23681063, registered 14 May 2024), and the LLC suffix matches the entity type on the filing. It holds no foreign filings, so its only registration is in the state where it was formed.

The filing names one person, Christopher S Lochte, as member and registered agent, and one address, the submitted Tucson office address. No website or third-party profile was found, so nothing outside the state filing presents the business under its name.

gaps.point: Whether the LLC is in good standing: Arizona reports the filing as active but publishes no good-standing sub-status.

body.text: The watchlist screen returned one result, on the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list: MAVERIKS, an entity with no aliases, matched against the business name. It is a different name from MAVERICK GAMES LLC, and nothing on the record ties it to the business or to Christopher S Lochte. The other thirteen lists screened returned nothing.
The PEP screen found no hits on the submitted individual or his relatives and close associates, and the adverse media screen returned no results.

gaps.point: Criminal history of Christopher S Lochte; the check was not ordered.
gaps.noAction: Not required to open a deposit account where the sanctions, PEP and adverse media screens are clear.

body.text: Industry classification points two ways. Its strongest NAICS code is Other Gambling Industries (713290), alongside Software Publishers and Miscellaneous Manufacturing, while the MCC is Computer Programming (7372); none is flagged high-risk and the prohibited-industry screen returned a non-prohibited category. No website or third-party profile was found, so nothing on the record shows whether the business publishes software games or operates games of chance.

The submitted office address, 7450 E Brooks Dr, Tucson, matches the filing and is a deliverable residential property, and the business is active in Arizona, the state of that address. A residential address that is also the registered agent's is ordinary for a single-member LLC run from home.

gaps.point: What the business sells and how it earns revenue, including whether any game involves real-money wagering or prizes.
Whether the business holds any gaming licence its activity requires in Arizona.
gaps.wouldAnswer: An Arizona Department of Gaming licence lookup, if the business offers wagering or prize-based games.

body.text: Christopher S Lochte, the submitted person, is matched to the Arizona filing as its member and registered agent, and is the only person the filing names. The structure is a single LLC with no business entities or third-party agents in its ownership or control.
No connected businesses were found.

gaps.point: Whether Christopher S Lochte is the sole member and what percentage he holds; the filing names members but not their interests.
Identity verification of Christopher S Lochte.

body.text: The business has no UCC or tax liens, no bankruptcy filings and no related litigation on record. For an LLC formed in May 2024 and run from a residence, an empty lien record is consistent with a business that has not financed equipment or taken secured credit.

gaps.point: Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming Christopher S Lochte; the people searches were not ordered.
gaps.noAction: Not required to open a deposit account where the business-level record is clear.

followUps.text:
Obtain a description of the products and revenue model, confirming whether any game involves real-money wagering or prizes, and collect the Arizona gaming licence if it does.
The strongest industry code is Other Gambling Industries while the MCC is Computer Programming, and no website or profile shows which.

Record the OFAC SDN result MAVERIKS as not a match to the business.
It was returned on the business name, but it is a different name and nothing on the record ties it to the business or its member.

Run KYC on Christopher S Lochte.
He is the member, registered agent and only person on the filing, and no identity verification is held.

Collect a beneficial ownership certification confirming Christopher S Lochte as sole member and stating his percentage.
The Arizona filing names him as member but not his interest.

Submit an RFI for a Certificate of Good Standing.
Arizona reports the filing as active but publishes no good-standing sub-status.

fishmonger don.name: Bank account opening
fishmonger don.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to a beneficial ownership certification, KYC on Donald B Mayfield, and proof that the business operates from its submitted San Francisco address.

body.text: FISHMONGER DON LLC holds one active domestic California filing (file 202035610124, registered 16 December 2020), in good standing. The submitted name matches the filing but for the LLC suffix, and the entity is registered as an LLC.
No website, TIN or phone was submitted. An unsubmitted website, fishmongerdon.com, presents the business under the submitted name.

The watchlist screen returned no hits across the 14 lists searched, including OFAC's. The PEP screen returned no hits on individuals or their relatives and close associates, and the adverse media screen returned no results.

gaps.point: Criminal history of Donald B Mayfield, the manager.
gaps.noAction: Not a standard requirement to open a deposit account where the watchlist, PEP and adverse media screens are clear.

body.text: The business classifies as a seafood seller: fish and seafood merchant wholesaler (NAICS 424460) and freezer and locker meat provisioner (MCC 5422), neither a prohibited nor a restricted industry. An insurance agency code (NAICS 524210) also scored highly; nothing else on the record supports it. The online LinkedIn, Facebook and Yelp profiles, the last a San Francisco listing with 33 reviews, describe the same seafood trade.

The business is active in California, the state of its submitted office address. That address, 2820 Taylor St, San Francisco, is a commercial property that is not on the filing, is undeliverable by USPS and is not shown on the website. The filing's only address is a residential mailing address in Fairfax, CA.
Selling seafood in California is licensed activity at the state and local level; no licence is on the record.

gaps.point: Whether the business operates from 2820 Taylor St, San Francisco.
Whether the business holds the licences required to buy and sell seafood in California.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A California Department of Fish and Wildlife commercial fish business licence lookup and the local retail food permit.

body.text: No people were submitted. The California filing names Donald B Mayfield as manager and as registered agent, the only person on the record; no entity owners or commercial registered agent appear.
No connections to other businesses were found, consistent with a single-manager LLC.

gaps.point: Who the LLC's members are, their percentages, and who is authorised to sign.
Identity verification of Donald B Mayfield.

body.text: The business has no UCC or tax liens, no bankruptcy filings and no related litigation on record.

gaps.point: Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming Donald B Mayfield.
gaps.noAction: Not required to open a deposit account where the business-level record is clear.

followUps.text:
Collect a beneficial ownership certification naming each member and percentage, and confirming Donald B Mayfield's role and who will sign.
No people were submitted and the filing names only a manager.

Run KYC on Donald B Mayfield.
He is the only person on the record and no identity verification is held.

Obtain proof of occupancy for 2820 Taylor St, San Francisco, such as a lease or utility bill.
The address is not on the filing, is undeliverable by USPS and is not shown on the website.

Collect the business's California commercial fish business licence and local food permit.
No check on the record covers licensing for seafood sales.

I am only able to offer FRESH day boat albacore a few times a year, if at all. Albacore are many miles off the coast so most boats fish for a number of days and either bring in frozen fish or fish that is a few days old. Albacore are plentiful, but getting day boat fish is truly exceptional. Danny is heading straight out and then right back in to hook us up with the absolute freshest albacore possible. DO NOT MISS OUT

Well I’m beaming today fish family! This is truly an iconic SF weekend! SF CRAB is open at last and boy, they are just gorgeous! Averaging 1.75-2 lbs each. Add to that, the 49ers are gonna push past the Packers as we all watch with big smiles feasting all the while on our favorite local delicacy! 🦀>🧀

HAVE A PARTY Y’ALL! Pick crab, shuck oysters, make poke bowls, snack on the finest salmon sashimi with your friends and family. This special weekend has been a long time coming! ENJOY! 

Big shouts to all the extremely hard-working folks out on the water and on the docks and my team, working feverishly to bring you all the very best!
McFARLAND SPRINGS CA NATIVE RAINBOW TROUT           Cold smoked (lox)
The most local tuna in town. ALBACORE ~ Fatty, oily, rich, delicious ~ Monterey Bay Aquarium’s Seafood Watch 💚Best Choice💚 USA troll caught, 0 bycatch
Grateful for my passionate, dedicated, thoughtful, sustainability minded, local partners who produce the most delightful morsels and items.
https://abnb.me/RlLAgROOQub I got a hankering to get back on the pier to share my passion and perspective with you! Yes there will be sea treats. Hope you can join a trip soon!

Guys, my all time favorite fish is coming in tonight - Day boat albacore tuna (troll caught, Ft. Bragg, Captain Danny Speirn) There is nothing like fresh, day boat albacore. The meat is so clean, tender, and beautiful. Day boat albacore makes some of the best poke, tataki, sashimi, sushi, pan seared fish you will ever eat. 

I am only able to offer FRESH day boat albacore a few times a year, if at all. Albacore are many miles off the coast so most boats fish for a number of days and either bring in frozen fish or fish that is a few days old. Albacore are plentiful, but getting day boat fish is truly exceptional. Danny is heading straight out and then right back in to hook us up with the absolute freshest albacore possible. DO NOT MISS OUT

Did I mention these troll caught California albacore are on the Monterrey bay aquarium’s seafood watch best choice list?

change.org, pbc.name: Bank account opening
change.org, pbc.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. - Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

report.headline: Onboard subject to a beneficial ownership certification that identifies any parent entity, KYC on the signing officers, and a confirmed physical principal address.

body.text: CHANGE.ORG, PBC is a Delaware public benefit corporation formed on 8 September 2006 (file 4215439), and the submitted name matches its filings with a suffix consistent with a corporation. A PBC is a for-profit stock corporation whose charter carries a stated public benefit.
Delaware publishes no filing status, so the domestic filing carries none; New Jersey likewise publishes none for its foreign filing.

Four foreign registrations are active: California (as Change.org Corp) and Kentucky both show good standing, and Maryland and New York show active with no sub-status. Three are inactive: a terminated California registration under the former name CHANGE.ORG, INC., a withdrawn District of Columbia registration and an inactive Washington registration.
No website was submitted; the one found, change.org, shows the submitted business name.

The watchlist screen returned no hits across the 14 lists searched, including OFAC's SDN and Sectoral Sanctions lists and BIS's Entity and Denied Persons lists. The PEP screen found no hits on the submitted individuals, Benjamin Rattray, Anthony Sebro Jr. and Duncan Lockard, or on their relatives and close associates. The adverse media screen returned no results.

gaps.point: Criminal history on the submitted officers.
gaps.noAction: Not required to open a deposit account; sanctions, PEP and adverse media screens on the business and submitted officers are clear.

body.text: The business classifies as web search portals and other information services (NAICS 519290, MCC 7399), with secondary matches to social advocacy organisations (NAICS 813319) and subscription direct marketing (MCC 5968). The industry screen places none in a prohibited or restricted category, and none is a licensed activity; the record carries an active Los Angeles city business registration.
The website, change.org, is online and names the submitted person, and six third-party profiles, including Trustpilot, BBB, LinkedIn and Facebook, are online and describe the same platform.

The submitted office address matches the filings, is deliverable commercial property, and the business is active in California, where it sits. 383 Rhode Island St Ste 300, San Francisco appears on the Maryland and New York filings and is the physical address on the Los Angeles registration.

The other two submitted addresses are not operating premises: 548 Market St PMB 29993, San Francisco is a commercial mail receiving agency mailbox shared by more than 1,000 businesses, and 251 Little Falls Dr, Wilmington is the Delaware registered agent's address. The website shows an address different from the submitted one.

gaps.point: Where the business physically operates: two of three submitted addresses are a mailbox and a registered agent, and the address the website shows is not on the record.

body.text: The submitted people, Benjamin Rattray (CEO), Anthony Sebro Jr. (Secretary) and Duncan Lockard (CFO), are matched to the active California filing, and Rattray also to the active New York filing.

Five further people appear only on inactive filings: Eve Chaurand and Rahoul Seth on the terminated CHANGE.ORG, INC. registration, and Joe Greenstein, Lynn Taliento and Nickolas Bearlin-Allardice as governing persons on the Washington registration. C T Corporation System appears on the New York filing for service of process, as registered agent, not as an officer or owner.

As a PBC, the business is owned by shareholders, and no filing names any. Of 13 connected businesses, CHANGE.ORG WORLDWIDE, INC. shares Rattray, Seth and Chaurand and the 383 Rhode Island St office, and THE CHANGE.ORG CHARITABLE FOUNDATION, INC. shares Rattray, Lockard and the Market St mailbox. The other eleven connect only through the other businesses of former officers or non-submitted governing persons, or through registered agent addresses.

gaps.point: Who holds 25% or more of the PBC and who exercises control; the filings name officers but no shareholders.
Whether CHANGE.ORG WORLDWIDE, INC. owns or controls the PBC.
Identity verification of the submitted officers.

body.text: The business has no liens and no bankruptcy filings.

Four litigation records cover three cases, each naming the business as a defendant and none carrying a money judgment. Tavarez v. Change.org, PBC, a disability-discrimination suit filed in the Southern District of New York in November 2021, is open. In Sanon et al v. Meta Platforms, Inc. et al (Bronx County Supreme Court, filed August 2025, recorded both open and closed) and Siganporia v. Shreyas et al (Northern District of California, April 2025, closed), the business is one of many co-defendants alongside large technology platforms.

gaps.point: Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted officers.
gaps.noAction: Not required to open a deposit account where the business-level record is clear of liens and bankruptcies.

followUps.text:
Collect a beneficial ownership certification naming each 25% owner and a control person, with an ownership chart showing whether CHANGE.ORG WORLDWIDE, INC. sits above the PBC.
No filing names shareholders, and CHANGE.ORG WORLDWIDE, INC. shares the CEO and the Rhode Island St office.

Run KYC on the signing officers, Benjamin Rattray, Anthony Sebro Jr. and Duncan Lockard as submitted.
No identity verification is held for any of them.

Confirm the principal place of business as a physical address.
Two submitted addresses are a mailbox and a registered agent, and the website shows an address not on the record.

charm coffee llc.name: Bank account opening
charm coffee llc.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to a beneficial ownership certification, KYC on Michael N Ellenburg with the adverse media match cleared, and evidence of the trading location and its food facility permit.

body.text: CHARM COFFEE LLC holds one domestic California LLC filing under the submitted name (file 202205910316, registered 24 February 2022), active and in good standing. The name's LLC suffix matches the entity type on the filing.
No website or third-party profile was found, so no web source carries the business name. No TIN was submitted.

The watchlist screen returned no hits across the 14 OFAC, BIS and State Department lists searched, including the SDN list. The PEP screen found no hits on the submitted individual or their relatives and close associates.

The adverse media screen holds one match to Michael N Ellenburg, the registered agent and submitted person: a January 2023 negative story, "Suspect: Realtor Impersonator", carried by three US Virgin Islands outlets (St Croix Source, St Thomas Source, St. John Tradewinds News). It is tagged fraud, bribery and corruption, narcotics, weapons sales and other non-financial crime at low to moderate confidence. Nothing names the business, and nothing on the record ties the story to this Michael N Ellenburg beyond the name; the business and its only address are in San Diego.

gaps.point: Whether the January 2023 realtor-impersonation story concerns the submitted Michael N Ellenburg or a namesake.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A reviewer disposition of the article against his KYC identifiers (date of birth, residential history).

gaps.point: Criminal history of Michael N Ellenburg; the search was not ordered.
gaps.noAction: Not a standard requirement for a business deposit account; the adverse media disposition addresses the open name match.

body.text: The business classifies as a snack and nonalcoholic beverage bar (NAICS 722515) and, for card acceptance, a fast food restaurant (MCC 5814), consistent with a coffee business and outside high-risk and prohibited categories.

The submitted office address, 7980 Linda Vista Rd Apt 46, San Diego, matches the filing, is deliverable, and is a residential apartment; the business is active in California, the state of that address. For a food-service business a residential filing address is ordinarily the owner's home, not the premises, so the record does not show where it trades.
No website or third-party profile was found, so no web source corroborates the address, the person, or that the business is operating.

gaps.point: Where the business trades and whether it is operating; the only address is a residential apartment and there is no web presence.
Whether the business holds a current retail food facility health permit for its trading location.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A San Diego County Department of Environmental Health food facility permit lookup for the trading address.

body.text: The only person on the record is Michael N Ellenburg, the submitted person, matched to the filing as its registered agent. The filing lists no officers, members or managers, so neither his ownership nor his authority to sign is established.
No connected businesses were found and nothing on the record points to an entity owner; the structure reads as a single LLC.

gaps.point: Who the LLC's members are, their percentages, and Michael N Ellenburg's role beyond registered agent.
Identity verification of Michael N Ellenburg.

body.text: The business has no tax or UCC liens, no bankruptcy filings and no related litigation on record. For a food-service LLC formed in 2022, the record shows no secured financing and no debt enforcement.

gaps.point: Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming Michael N Ellenburg.
gaps.noAction: Not required to open a deposit account where the business-level record is clear.

followUps.text:
Collect a beneficial ownership certification naming each member, their percentage and the control person, and confirming Michael N Ellenburg's authority to sign.
The filing lists no members or officers and names him only as registered agent.

Run KYC on Michael N Ellenburg.
He is the only person on the record and no identity verification is held.

Disposition the adverse media match against his KYC identifiers.
Three US Virgin Islands outlets carry one January 2023 realtor-impersonation story matched to his name only.

Obtain the address the business trades from and evidence that it is operating, such as a lease or recent processing statements.
The only address is a residential apartment and no website or third-party profile was found.

Verify a current San Diego County food facility health permit for that location.
No check on the record covers food-service permits.

the mala market, llc.name: Bank account opening
the mala market, llc.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to a beneficial ownership certification, KYC and screening of the owners and signers, and the business's operating address.

body.text: THE MALA MARKET, LLC is a Tennessee domestic LLC (file 000923109), registered 14 September 2017 under the submitted name. It is its only filing, and it is active and in good standing.

The filing names Registered Agents Inc as registered agent and lists no officers or entity owners. No TIN, website, profile or phone was submitted. An unsubmitted website, themalamarket.com, shows a name similar to the legal name; its domain was registered in September 2016, a year before formation.
The watchlist screen on the business returned no hits across the OFAC, BIS and State Department lists, and the adverse media screen returned no results.
The PEP screen returned no hits. No individuals are submitted or listed on the filing, so no owner or signer has yet been screened for sanctions, PEP status or adverse media.

gaps.point: Sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening of the beneficial owners and signers, once identified.
Criminal history of the owners and signers; the search was not ordered.
gaps.noAction: Not required to open a deposit account, and no individuals are yet identified to search.

body.text: The business classifies as a specialty food seller, as a grocery merchant wholesaler (NAICS 424490) and specialty food store (MCC 5499), and is not classified in a prohibited or restricted industry. Its website is an online Shopify storefront selling Sichuan ingredients, and an online Trustpilot profile categorises it as an Asian grocery and spice store.

The submitted office address, 116 Agnes Rd Ste 200, Knoxville, matches the filing and is a deliverable commercial property, but it is the registered agent's address and the website does not show it. The business is active in Tennessee, the state of that address. The filing's other address is a residential mailing address in Nashville. For an online retailer a registered-agent office is common, but it leaves where the business operates and holds stock off the record.

gaps.point: Where the business operates and holds inventory; the submitted office address is its registered agent's.
Whether the business holds any food-establishment permit its operating location requires.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A licence search against the operating address, or a copy of any state food permit held.

body.text: No owners, officers or signers are submitted, and the Tennessee filing lists none; it names only Registered Agents Inc, a commercial registered agent and not an owner. Nothing on the record shows an entity owner or layered structure, but the structure is unknown until the owners are declared.

One connected business, Latex Foam International LLC, shares the filing's Nashville mailing address, a residential property. A shared residential mailing address points to a common owner or household, which the record does not establish.

gaps.point: Who owns and controls the LLC, their percentages, and who will sign on the account.
Identity verification of the beneficial owners and signers.
Whether Latex Foam International LLC shares ownership with the business.

body.text: The business has no liens, no bankruptcy filings and no related litigation on record, nine years after formation.

gaps.point: Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the owners.
gaps.noAction: No individuals are identified, and it is not required for a deposit account where the business-level record is clear.

followUps.text:
Collect a beneficial ownership certification naming each owner, their percentage and the authorised signers, and confirming any common ownership with Latex Foam International LLC.
No people are submitted or on the Tennessee filing, and that business shares the filing's residential mailing address.

Run KYC and sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening on each owner and signer.
The screenings so far cover the business only.

Collect the address the business operates and ships from, with any food-establishment permit held for it.
The submitted office address is the registered agent's and the website shows no address.

old stuff vintage sales llc.name: Bank account opening
old stuff vintage sales llc.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Do not onboard while the Wisconsin LLC is administratively dissolved; reconsider on evidence of reinstatement, a beneficial ownership certification and KYC on Jon J Bram.

body.text: OLD STUFF VINTAGE SALES LLC is a Wisconsin LLC, registered on 14 September 2023 under file O043535, and the filing carries the submitted name.

That domestic filing is the business's only one and is administratively dissolved, so the business holds no active Secretary of State filing anywhere. A dissolved LLC's authority is limited to winding up its affairs until the state reinstates it.
An unsubmitted website presents the business under a name similar to the legal name.
The watchlist screen, run across 14 sanctions and export-control lists including OFAC, returned no hits.
The PEP screen returned no hits on the submitted individual, Jon J Bram, or his relatives and close associates, and the adverse media screen returned no results.

gaps.point: Criminal history on Jon J Bram; the check was not ordered.
gaps.noAction: Not a standard requirement for a business deposit account where the sanctions, PEP and adverse media screens are clear.

body.text: The business classifies as a used merchandise retailer (NAICS 459510; MCC 5932, antique shops), and the industry screen returned no hits against prohibited or restricted categories.

A website was found and was online, but it shows neither the submitted address nor the submitted person, and no third-party profiles were found. The online footprint therefore rests on the website alone.

The submitted office address in Grantsburg, Wisconsin matches the filing and is a deliverable residential property, which is ordinary for a small home-based reseller. The business is inactive in that state.

gaps.point: Whether the business holds any secondhand or antique dealer licence its municipality requires.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A licence lookup with the Grantsburg, Wisconsin municipal clerk, or a copy of the licence from the customer.

body.text: Jon J Bram, the submitted person, is matched to the Wisconsin filing, which names him as registered agent and lists no officers or members. His ownership and control of the LLC are not on the record.
No connected businesses were found, so the record shows a single-entity LLC with no business owners or intermediate layers.

gaps.point: Who the LLC's members are, their percentages, and whether Jon J Bram is an owner or signer beyond registered agent.
Identity verification of Jon J Bram.

body.text: The business has no liens, no bankruptcy filings and no related litigation on record.

gaps.point: Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming Jon J Bram.
gaps.noAction: Not required to open a deposit account where the business-level record is clear.

followUps.text:
Obtain evidence that Wisconsin has reinstated the LLC, such as a current Certificate of Status, before the account opens.
Its only filing is administratively dissolved and it holds no active filing anywhere.

Collect a beneficial ownership certification naming each member, their percentage and who will sign on the account.
The filing lists no members or officers, and Jon J Bram appears only as registered agent.

Run KYC on Jon J Bram.
He is the only person submitted and no identity verification is held.

Confirm whether the business needs a municipal secondhand or antique dealer licence and, if so, collect it.
It resells used merchandise and no licence check is on the record.
