sorenson communications, llc.name: Bank account opening
sorenson communications, llc.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to evidence of an active home-state formation in good standing, a beneficial ownership certification reaching the individuals behind SCI HOLDINGS LLC, KYC on the signers, and disposition of the PEP results against David Johnson.

body.text: The submitted name matches the Utah domestic filing of SORENSON COMMUNICATIONS, LLC (file 4737021-0142, registered 24 March 2000), and the website sorenson.com, not submitted, shows the same name. The Utah filing is inactive with the status Expired and lists no officers.

27 of the 28 filings on the record are inactive. The one active filing is a Mississippi foreign registration in good standing (file 959722, 2009) under Sorenson Communications, Limited Liability Company. The other 26 foreign filings are under SORENSON COMMUNICATIONS, INC. and read Withdrawn, Converted, Revoked or Inactive, consistent with a predecessor corporation that converted to the LLC.
No TIN, phone or DBA was submitted.

gaps.point: Where the LLC is currently formed and whether that formation is active and in good standing. The Utah domestic filing has expired, and an active foreign registration presupposes a home-state formation the record does not hold; Utah publishes no good-standing sub-status.

body.text: No watchlist result is valid. The two returned are near-misses on names found on the filings, not on the business or the submitted people: James Lee on the State Department AECA/ITAR debarred list, against director James Lee Sorenson, whose middle name is Lee; and PARK, Jin Hyok on the OFAC SDN list, against director David Johnson through the alias DAVID, Andoson.

The PEP screen returned three results, all linked to David Johnson, a director on ten inactive foreign filings and on the CaptionCall, LLC and Sorenson Interpretive Services, LLC connections: Dave David Howard Johnson, David Johnson and Corey Johnson. The results carry no identifiers or source links. None is linked to Reed Steiner or Scott Sorensen.

No adverse media was returned against the business name, Reed Steiner or Scott Sorensen. Four names found on the record returned articles, each matched on the name alone: David Johnson (an obituary, a Utah county party chairman charged with child abuse, and human-trafficking pleas in Santa Barbara); Darren Richman, a director on the Arizona and Missouri filings (a securities class action against F45 Training Holdings and a dispute at a credit manager); Nathan Russell, named on Form 5500 filings (an Iowa murder trial); and WITHDRAWN, a status word parsed as the secretary's name on the Illinois filing, which matched unrelated articles containing that word.

gaps.point: Whether David Johnson is a current director or controller and, if so, whether the PEP results and the articles concern him or namesakes.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A reviewer disposition of the three PEP results and the articles against his date of birth and residential address, once his current role is confirmed.

gaps.point: Criminal history of the submitted people.
gaps.noAction: Not ordered and not required to open a deposit account; no screening result on the submitted people points to it.

body.text: The business classifies as Translation and Interpretation Services (NAICS 541930) with telecommunication services (MCC 4814) secondary, outside high-risk and prohibited categories. The online website, titled for language services and ASL interpreting, and the online LinkedIn, BBB, X, Trustpilot and Google profiles describe the same line of work; Google categorises it as a deaf service and BBB as assistive telecommunications equipment.

The submitted office, 4192 S Riverboat Rd, Salt Lake City, matches the filings and the website and is a deliverable commercial property shared by 21 businesses. The second submitted address, 2 N Jackson St Ste 605, Montgomery, Alabama, is a registered agent address. The business is inactive in Utah, the state of its office, as its only Utah filing has expired. The website names people other than the submitted officers.

gaps.point: Whether the LLC holds active authority to do business in Utah, where its office is.
Whether the business holds any service registrations its interpreting and telecommunication services require.
gaps.wouldAnswer: The business's FCC registration and any state interpreter-service authorisations.
gaps.noAction: The industry classifies outside high-risk and prohibited categories, and opening the account does not turn on a service licence.

body.text: Reed Steiner (chief financial officer, secretary, treasurer, director) and Scott Sorensen (chief executive officer, president) are matched to the filings, but only to the inactive foreign filings of SORENSON COMMUNICATIONS, INC. The Utah domestic filing lists no officers and the active Mississippi filing names only R. Scott Wood, so no active filing evidences either submitted officer's current role.

The submitted owner is SCI HOLDINGS LLC, an entity that appears on no filing on the record, so ownership runs through at least one holding company and the individuals behind it are not identified. Of eight connections, three bear on the structure: SORENSON HOLDINGS, LLC, also a name on the record, whose people Keith Luh and James V Continenza are directors on the Arizona and Missouri filings; and CAPTIONCALL, LLC and SORENSON INTERPRETIVE SERVICES, LLC, which share the submitted officers and name this business as a party. The remaining five share only one individual each with the business.

gaps.point: Who owns SCI HOLDINGS LLC, whether SORENSON HOLDINGS, LLC sits in the chain, and which individuals hold 25% or more.
Who currently controls the LLC and holds signing authority, as the submitted officers are evidenced only on inactive predecessor filings.
Identity verification of Reed Steiner, Scott Sorensen and any individual beneficial owner.

body.text: Two UCC filings are open in Utah against the business: one filed 19 April 2024 by Oaktree Fund Administration LLC as administrative agent and one filed 30 April 2019 by Credit Suisse AG Cayman Islands Branch as collateral agent, both lapsing in 2029, with no collateral described on the record. The twelve closed filings since 2006 are mostly held by collateral agents, a pattern consistent with successive syndicated secured facilities. There are no tax liens and no bankruptcy filings.

Of ten litigation records, six are open employment matters naming the business as defendant or employer, filed December 2025 to June 2026: three filings by Norima Lonesky in California, one a PAGA representative action; two by David Gunsauls in California; and a Florida workers' compensation claim by Tricia A. Motes. A 2025 NLRB charge involving the Office and Professional Employees International Union is closed. In the other three the business is garnishee on employees' consumer debts. No money judgment is entered against the business.

gaps.point: What the open Oaktree and Credit Suisse filings secure, and whether the facilities require control over the business's deposit accounts.
Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people.
gaps.noAction: Not required to open a deposit account where the business-level record is read in full.

followUps.text:
Collect the LLC's current certificate of formation, a Certificate of Good Standing from its home state and evidence of authority to do business in Utah.
The Utah domestic filing has expired and the only active filing is a Mississippi foreign registration.

Collect a beneficial ownership certification naming each individual owning 25% or more through SCI HOLDINGS LLC and the current control person and signers.
SCI HOLDINGS LLC is on no filing, and the submitted officers appear only on inactive predecessor filings.

Run KYC on Reed Steiner, Scott Sorensen and each individual owner the certification names.
No identity verification is held.

Confirm whether David Johnson is a current director or controller and, if so, disposition the three PEP results and his articles against his identifiers.
All three PEP results are linked to him and carry no identifiers.

Ask whether the Oaktree or Credit Suisse facility requires a deposit account control agreement over the new account.
Both UCC filings are open and describe no collateral.

modern realty inc.name: Bank account opening
modern realty inc.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to confirming the litigation records belong to this Utah corporation, KYC and a beneficial ownership certification covering its two officers, a Utah good-standing certificate and a real estate licence check.

body.text: MODERN REALTY INC holds one active domestic Utah filing (file 12160647-0142, registered 10 February 2021) under the submitted name, as a corporation. The filing lists the submitted office address in Vernal, Utah, and no foreign filings were found.

The filing names two officers, Michael Eskelson and Jacob Selby, both submitted; Michael Eskelson also serves as registered agent, so no third-party agent sits on the record. No website or third-party profile was found, so the business name is not corroborated anywhere online.

gaps.point: Whether the corporation is in good standing: Utah publishes an active status but no good-standing sub-status.

body.text: The watchlist screen returned no hits across the 14 lists searched, including OFAC SDN, Sectoral Sanctions and Foreign Sanctions Evaders and the BIS Entity and Denied Persons lists. The PEP screen found no hits on the submitted individuals, Michael Eskelson and Jacob Selby, or on their relatives and close associates.
The adverse media screen returned no results.

gaps.point: Criminal history on Michael Eskelson and Jacob Selby was not ordered.
gaps.noAction: Not a standard account-opening check; the sanctions, PEP and adverse media screens on both officers ran and were clear.

body.text: The business classifies as an office of real estate agents and brokers (NAICS 531210; MCC 6513, real estate agents and managers, rentals), which the industry screen does not place in a prohibited or restricted category. Real estate brokerage is licensed activity in Utah, and no licence is on the record.

The submitted office address, 1188 S 1500 W, Vernal, matches the filing and is a deliverable commercial property, and the business is active in Utah, where that office sits. The other four filing addresses are residential properties in Vernal.
No website and no third-party profile were found, so nothing online describes the business's activity, address or people.

gaps.point: Whether the business holds a current Utah real estate brokerage licence, and who its principal broker is.

body.text: Both submitted people are matched to the state filing: Michael Eskelson as president, director and registered agent, and Jacob Selby as vice president and director. No business entity or third-party agent appears as an owner or officer. As a corporation, its owners are shareholders, which the Utah filing does not publish.

All 13 connections run through the two officers. Modern Realty Property Management, LLC and Safari Group, LLC share both officers and the primary office address; the other eleven, including Selby Real Estate Inc., H&M Real Estate Corp and several Vernal construction firms, share one officer each. These are common-officer affiliates, not owners on the record.

gaps.point: Who owns the corporation's shares, and in what percentages.
Identity verification of Michael Eskelson and Jacob Selby as individuals.

body.text: UCC and tax lien searches found no liens, and no bankruptcy filings were found.

Ten cases name a Modern Realty, Inc., all in New Jersey, Texas and Illinois courts, none in Utah, and six filed before this corporation was formed in February 2021. Three are open: a 2024 New Jersey commercial eviction it brought, a related 2024 New Jersey commercial case naming it as defendant, and a 2018 federal insurance declaratory action in Illinois naming it alongside Modern Homes, Inc. The seven closed cases are four New Jersey Tax Court appeals against Carlstadt Borough and three Texas cases, two ending in judgment in its favour; no money judgment against it is recorded.

gaps.point: Whether the ten cases concern this Utah corporation or a same-named business elsewhere.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A review of each case's party details against the Utah filing's officers and addresses.

gaps.point: Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming Michael Eskelson or Jacob Selby were not ordered.
gaps.noAction: Officers' personal filings are not required to open a business account; the business-level searches ran.

followUps.text: Confirm whether the ten litigation records concern this business; all sit in New Jersey, Texas and Illinois courts, and six predate its 2021 Utah formation.
Obtain a beneficial ownership certification naming each 25% shareholder and the control person, as the Utah filing names officers but not shareholders.
Run KYC on Michael Eskelson and Jacob Selby, the corporation's two officers and directors.
Submit an RFI for a Utah Certificate of Existence, as Utah publishes an active status but no good-standing sub-status.
Verify a current Utah real estate brokerage licence for the business and its principal broker; none is on the record.
Request the business's website or listing profiles, or a description of its brokerage activity, as no web presence was found.

supabase, inc..name: Bank account opening
supabase, inc..brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to a beneficial ownership certification, KYC on the officers with the adverse media on Anthony Wilson and Richard Tatum cleared, evidence the 2023 Workers' Compensation Board judgment is satisfied, and an operating address.

body.text: SUPABASE, INC. is a Delaware corporation, file 7816270, formed 24 January 2020, and the submitted name matches the filing. Delaware publishes no status or sub-status for the domestic filing. The foreign filings in Alabama, Arizona and California are active, and California reports the corporation in good standing.

Unsubmitted, the record holds a website, supabase.com, that shows the business name, and an industry classification of software publisher. The Arizona filing names one unsubmitted director, Caryn Marooney. The registered agents on the filings, Rocket Lawyer Corporate Services, ISL Inc and Incorporating Services, hold no owner or officer role, and no business entity is listed as one.

The watchlist screen returned no hits across the 14 OFAC, BIS and State Department lists screened, including the SDN list. The PEP screen returned no hits on the submitted individuals or their relatives and close associates.

Adverse media returned negative items on three people, each at a 0.87 name-match score; no result is keyed to the business itself. For Anthony Wilson, a submitted director, it is a 2014 ABC Australia report of a serial armed robber of that name having a life sentence quashed (weapons, high confidence); his other five items are unrelated local news and listings. For Richard Tatum, who appears on the business's Form 5500 but was not submitted, they are 2025 Columbus, Ohio reports of police shooting an armed man of that name and a Fourth Circuit case, Richard Tatum v. Chamber of Commerce, tagged fraud and money laundering at moderate confidence.

For Paul Copplestone, the one negative item is a Tsecurity article on OpenClaw patching a remote-code-execution flaw, tagged cybercrime at high confidence; his other item reports a Supabase funding round. Nothing on the record ties any of these items to the individuals beyond the name.

gaps.point: Whether the armed-robbery, police-shooting and court items concern Anthony Wilson and Richard Tatum or namesakes, and whether the OpenClaw article concerns the business.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A reviewer disposition of each item against the individual's KYC identifiers (date of birth, residence).

gaps.point: Criminal history of the submitted people.
gaps.noAction: Not ordered and not required to open a deposit account; the adverse media items are dispositioned against KYC identifiers.

body.text: The business classifies as a software publisher (NAICS 513210; MCC 7372, computer programming), outside high-risk and prohibited categories. The website was online and presents a Postgres development platform, and the six third-party profiles found (LinkedIn, X, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and Trustpilot) are online. Software publishing requires no industry licence; the record holds an active San Francisco city registration under the name.

The submitted office address matches a filing and is a deliverable commercial property, but it is a registered agent address, as are the other submitted addresses in Dover and Newark, Delaware and Phoenix, each used by more than 10,000 businesses. The website shows a different address and names people other than the submitted officers, and the Alabama filing lists a Singapore address as primary. No operating address is on the record.

gaps.point: Where the business operates: every submitted address is a registered agent address, and the website and the Alabama filing show other addresses.

body.text: Paul Copplestone, submitted, is matched to the Arizona and California filings as chief executive officer, chief financial officer, secretary and director; Anthony Wilson and Arun Mathew, both submitted, are directors on the Arizona filing. Caryn Marooney is a further director on that filing who was not submitted, and Richard Tatum appears on the business's 2025 Form 5500 with no stated role.

No business connections were found and no entity is listed as an owner or officer. The filings of a corporation name officers and directors but not shareholders, so the beneficial owners and their percentages are not on the record.

gaps.point: Who holds 25% or more of the corporation and who is its control person.
Identity verification of the submitted officers and the account signer.

body.text: The business has no liens and no bankruptcy filings. It is the defendant in one open case, Workers' Compensation Board of the State of New York v. SUPABASE INC (908717-23, Albany County Supreme Court), filed 14 September 2023 as a wage claim, with a judgment entered by the clerk on 18 September 2023; the record carries no judgment amount.

gaps.point: The amount of the 2023 Workers' Compensation Board judgment and whether it has been satisfied.
Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people.
gaps.noAction: Not ordered and not required to open a deposit account for a corporation; the business-level records were searched.

followUps.text:
Collect a beneficial ownership certification naming each 25% owner and the control person, and confirming the roles of Caryn Marooney and Richard Tatum.
The filings name officers and directors but no shareholders; Caryn Marooney is an unsubmitted director and Richard Tatum appears only on the Form 5500.

Run KYC on Paul Copplestone, Anthony Wilson and Arun Mathew, and on any owner the certification names.
No identity verification is held on the record.

Clear the negative adverse media against each individual's KYC identifiers.
A 2014 armed-robbery report matches Anthony Wilson, and 2025 police-shooting reports and a fraud-tagged court case match Richard Tatum, by name only.

Obtain the amount of the Workers' Compensation Board judgment entered 18 September 2023 and evidence it has been satisfied.
The New York wage-claim case is open and the record carries no amount.

Collect the business's principal operating address.
Every submitted address is a registered agent address; the website shows another and the Alabama filing lists Singapore.

zions bank.name: Bank account opening
zions bank.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to confirming ZB, National Association's federal bank charter and current legal name, identifying and verifying the authorised signers, and documenting the Entity List hit as a false positive.

body.text: ZIONS BANK holds one domestic Idaho filing under the submitted name (file 557804, registered 19 February 2016), active and in good standing with the status Active-Current. It is the only filing on the record.

The filing carries no entity type and lists a single owner, ZB, National Association, at a Salt Lake City, Utah mailing address. It therefore evidences the name as held by that bank rather than the formation of a separate entity, and no formation record for ZB, National Association itself is on file; a national association is chartered federally, not by a Secretary of State.
The website found for the business, zionsbank.com, shows the submitted business name.

gaps.point: The legal existence and current name of ZB, National Association, the entity that owns the name and would hold the account.
gaps.wouldAnswer: An OCC charter record or certificate of corporate existence for ZB, National Association, showing its current legal name.

body.text: The watchlist screen returned one hit across fourteen lists, on the BIS Entity List, matched to the submitted owner ZB, National Association. The listed party is State Concern National Production and Agricultural Association Massandra, with four aliases in the same form; the screen classes it as not a valid hit. No list returned a hit on the business name, and OFAC's SDN and other OFAC lists returned none.
The PEP screen found no hits on the submitted party or relatives and close associates, and the adverse media screen returned no results.

gaps.point: A documented disposition of the Entity List hit against ZB, National Association.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A reviewer disposition in the onboarding file comparing the listed party's name, aliases and identifiers with the owner.

gaps.point: Criminal history of the people behind the business.
gaps.noAction: No natural person is submitted; the only party on the application is a corporate owner.

body.text: The business classifies as commercial banking (NAICS 522110, MCC 6011); the industry screen returned no hits and the prohibited-industry classification is other non-prohibited. The website is online, and the third-party profiles, including BBB listings categorised as a bank, are online and describe the same line of work. The customer is therefore itself a deposit-taking institution.

The submitted office address, 1 S Main St, Salt Lake City, Utah, matches the filing and the website, and is a deliverable commercial property. The business holds no registration in Utah, the state of that address; its only filing is in Idaho. The website names people other than the submitted party, which is a corporate owner.

gaps.point: Whether ZB, National Association holds a current bank charter and deposit insurance, the authority under which a bank operates in Utah without a state registration.
gaps.wouldAnswer: An OCC charter lookup and FDIC BankFind certificate for ZB, National Association.

body.text: The only submitted party, ZB, National Association, is matched to the Idaho filing as its owner. Court captions on the record name the same party as Zions Bancorporation, N.A., formerly known as ZB, N.A., doing business as Zions First National Bank, so the owner's name on the filing may be a former one.

One connection was found: ZIONS FIRST NATIONAL BANK, at 0.991 confidence, sharing the same owner and the 1 S Main St mailing address. It reads as another name of the same bank rather than a separate owner.
No natural person is submitted and no identity verification is held, so the record names no signer or control person.

gaps.point: Whether the customer is a federally regulated bank excluded from beneficial ownership certification, or a legal entity customer whose 25% owners and control person must be certified.
gaps.wouldAnswer: Confirmation of the charter, then either the regulated-bank exclusion or a certification.

gaps.point: Who is authorised to act for the bank on the account, and their identity verification.

body.text: Two open Utah UCC filings are on record, both filed 25 September 2007 under the same file number and lapsing 25 September 2027, likely one filing indexed twice. The secured party is the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco and the debtors are the bank's names, including ZB N A and Zions First National Bank; no collateral or amount is stated. A filing in favour of a Reserve Bank is ordinary for a depository institution pledging collateral.

Ten litigations are on record, none with a money judgment against the business. It is plaintiff in two collection matters, including an Arizona judgment of $5,825.01 principal against an individual, and garnishee in one open Pennsylvania matter. It is a co-defendant or appellee in the rest: two closed matters dismissed in 2024, open Idaho and Ninth Circuit appeals in the Shoemaker bankruptcy matter, and multi-defendant pro se suits by Livia Scotto, one on appeal.
The business has no bankruptcy filings.

gaps.point: Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the people behind the business.
gaps.noAction: No natural person is submitted, and the business-level record carries no judgment against it.

followUps.text:
Verify ZB, National Association's charter, current legal name and FDIC certificate on the OCC and FDIC records.
The Idaho filing is a name owned by that bank, court records name it Zions Bancorporation, N.A., formerly ZB, N.A., and no state registration covers its Utah office.

Collect a board resolution or incumbency certificate naming the authorised signers, and run KYC on each.
No natural person is submitted and no identity verification is held.

Apply the regulated-bank exclusion to beneficial ownership once the charter is confirmed; otherwise collect a certification of 25% owners and a control person.
The only party on record is the corporate owner.

Record a disposition of the BIS Entity List hit against ZB, National Association.
The listed party is State Concern National Production and Agricultural Association Massandra, and the screen classes it as not valid.

recent_posts.text: For their exceptional contributions and hard work, we congratulate this year’s “Excellence … It Starts With Me” award winners, the Roy W. Simmons Community Service Award recipient, and the 363 employees celebrating years of service milestones.

Bob Wilson and Rick Wilson have joined Zions Wealth as senior vice presidents and wealth professionals and will be supported by client account service associates Jannet Sheehan and Heather Sullivan.

The team is based at Zions Bank’s Idaho headquarters at Eighth and Main in downtown Boise and will serve clients in Western and North Idaho and the Wood River Valley.

Rick and Bob, who are twin brothers, bring more than 30 years of experience in the financial services industry to the positions, most recently as wealth advisors and market managers at ICCU. 

As certified Chartered Retirement Planning Counselors, they specialize in building relationships with high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth individuals, families and business owners, and have extensive experience serving complex client needs through a disciplined approach to wealth management practices.

Investment Products: Not FDIC Insured | No Bank Guarantee | May Lose Value

We’re proud of Catherine Arik, Eastern Idaho/Wyoming region president, who was honored as one of the Idaho Business Review’s “Women of the Year.”

She was recognized for helping to shape Idaho’s economic and community well-being through her outstanding leadership, mentoring efforts and community involvement.

As region president, she’s focused on building a strong, empowered team of employees to provide a positive experience for clients. Her commitment to supporting small businesses has contributed to Zions Bank’s ranking as the no. 1 7(a) SBA lender in Idaho in 2023, 2024 and 2025.

Arik is a board member for the Regional Economic Development for Eastern Idaho (REDI) and serves as a mentor for People Helping People, a nonprofit organization that works to help single mothers obtain financial self-sufficiency. 

Congratulations, Catherine, and thanks for all you do for our clients and communities!

It’s been 20 years since Eli Madrigal opened her first Rancho Markets grocery store with the help of an SBA loan from Zions Bank.

Today, the independently owned, Hispanic-focused grocery chain has nine locations across the Wasatch Front and a new Idaho store in development.

Read about Eli’s entrepreneurial insight and guidance for small business owners: https://www.zionsbank.com/personal/community/business-feed/small-business-success-rancho-markets/

The golden goose of finances may not be a goose at all… but rather, a grandparent. In honor of Grandparents Day, our bankers share generational money lessons that stuck with them. 

https://www.zionsbank.com/personal/community/personal-finance-feed/golden-financial-guidance-from-grandparents/

We're proud to support the Utah 9/11 Project alongside South Jordan City and the Major Brent Taylor Foundation. This week we presented a $10,000 check to Mayor Dawn Ramsey and Jennie Taylor, foundation CEO and wife of the late Major Brent Taylor.

Now through Sept. 14, join us in commemorating the anniversary of 9/11 at the Bastian Agricultural Center in South Jordan. The event includes a free immersive museum, community resource fair, and Touch-a-Truck exhibit. Learn more at majorbrenttaylor.com.

Today we commemorated Patriot Day with a ruck/walk/run organized by our Military and Veterans Employee Forum to honor and remember those affected by the events of Sept. 11, 2001. 

Participants chose to ruck, walk or run a 2- or 4-mile course around the Zions Technology Center in Midvale.⁠
⁠
We’re grateful to our forum members and all participants for creating a meaningful opportunity to come together in reflection and unity. #NeverForget

We invest in our people and their development because their growth propels us all forward.

We’re proud of these Zions Bankers who recently completed advanced courses of study to deepen their banking knowledge and leadership skills.

Brad Brockbank, Jake Christensen, Courtney Clark, Matt Gibbons, Chad Gourley, Dave Heer, Lance Johnson, Kristiane Koontz, Thuy N La, Ryan Maughan, Jared Nicholson, Ben Penrod, Angela Scott, Mark Siegel and Naeim Sobhani graduated from Pacific Coast Banking School.

Katie Black, Kristen McCabe, Kenny Miller, Chad Park, Mikey Reynolds, Lauren Sur, Natalie Thompson and Jennifer Troyan graduated from the ABA Stonier Graduate School of Banking Graduate School of Banking.

Congratulations, graduates!

We’re hiring!

As we continue to expand our services to businesses and individuals across Teton County — and beyond — we are in search of talented financial services professionals. Join our growing and well-known local team that will open Zions Bank’s stunning new Highway 89 location in spring 2027.

NOW HIRING:

Apply online at careers.zionsbank.com and search by job number. Zions Bank is an equal opportunity employer.

sprig technologies inc..name: Bank account opening
sprig technologies inc..brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

report.headline: Onboard subject to evidence that the Delaware filing for MIXBOARD INC. is this corporation, a beneficial ownership certification, KYC on Ryan Glasgow, disposition of the name-only adverse media and a confirmed physical operating address.

body.text: SPRIG TECHNOLOGIES INC. is a Delaware corporation. Its California foreign filing (C4312456, registered 2019-09-05) carries the submitted name and is active and in good standing.

No domestic filing is on this record. The Delaware domestic filing sits on a linked record under MIXBOARD INC. (#6473823), which shares Ryan Glasgow and three San Francisco addresses, and the San Francisco business registration lists Sprig Technologies Inc as a DBA of Mixboard Inc. on an account open since 2017, alongside the earlier DBA Userleap Inc. That reads as one corporation that has changed its name, but nothing on the record shows the Delaware name change.
The website, sprig.com, was found without being submitted and shows the submitted business name.

gaps.point: Whether the Delaware filing for MIXBOARD INC. (#6473823) is this corporation under its former name.

body.text: The watchlist screen returned no hits across the 14 lists searched, including the OFAC SDN list. The PEP screen found no hits on the submitted individual or on relatives and close associates.

Adverse media returned nothing on the business name. It returned two person-level results, each at a 0.87 name-match score. For Ryan Glasgow, one Guyana Times report of a man jailed for theft of a brush cutter, tagged fraud, bribery and corruption at moderate confidence; nothing in it ties the report to him or the business beyond the name.

For Richard Tatum, who appears on the 2025 Form 5500 without a title, six items: Columbus Dispatch and World News reports of Columbus, Ohio police shooting an armed suspect named Richard Tatum in January 2025, tagged weapons at high confidence, and two Fourth Circuit cases, Tatum v. RJR Pension Investment Committee and Tatum v. Chamber of Commerce, tagged fraud and money laundering at moderate confidence. None references the business, its addresses or its line of work.

gaps.point: Whether the adverse media items concern the Ryan Glasgow and Richard Tatum on this record or namesakes.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A reviewer disposition of each item against the individuals' KYC identifiers (date of birth, residential address).

gaps.point: Criminal history of the individuals on the record.
gaps.noAction: Not a standard requirement for a business deposit account; the watchlist and PEP screens are clear.

body.text: The business classifies as software and market research (MCC 7372; NAICS 541910 and 513210), outside high-risk and prohibited categories. The website, sprig.com, is online and describes an enterprise research platform; a Trustpilot profile categorising it as a software company and an X profile for Ryan Glasgow are online.
Software publishing and market research are not licensed activities, so no licence is expected and none is on the record.

The submitted office address, 2021 Fillmore St PMB 86, San Francisco, matches the record and is deliverable, but is zoned as a commercial mail receiving agency, so it is a mailbox rather than premises. The business is active in California, the website shows an address within 0.2 miles of the submitted office address and names Ryan Glasgow, and the California filing and current San Francisco registration list 71 Stevenson St Ste 600.

gaps.point: Whether the business operates from 71 Stevenson St Ste 600 or other physical premises.

body.text: Ryan Glasgow, the submitted person, is matched to the California filing, which names him chief executive officer, chief financial officer, secretary and registered agent; he is the only officer on the record. Richard Tatum appears on the 2025 Form 5500 plan filing with no title.

As a Delaware corporation, its filings publish officers but no shareholders, so beneficial owners are not on the record. The San Francisco registration names Mixboard Inc. as owner of the Sprig Technologies name; if Mixboard is a separate company rather than a former name, ownership runs through a second entity.

The four connections share an address only, with no people in common: IRONCLAD, INC. at 71 Stevenson St Ste 600, and CHARACTER SF, LLC, VASANT THOROUGHBRED FARMS, LLC and UNIVERSITY HEIGHTS APARTMENTS, LLC at 447 Battery St Fl 3, the registered agent address on the California filing.

gaps.point: Who holds 25% or more of the corporation, and whether Mixboard Inc. sits in the ownership chain.
Identity verification of Ryan Glasgow as control person and signer.

body.text: No liens and no bankruptcy filings are on record.

Two cases name the business as defendant. A Wisconsin Department of Workforce Development unemployment-tax warrant (Dane County, 2024UC001244) produced a $1,893.48 judgment, fully satisfied on 2025-03-03. Rodriguez v Sprig Technologies Inc (San Diego County Superior Court, 25CU058027C), a civil rights claim filed 2025-10-27 that also names www.sprig.com, is open with no judgment.

gaps.point: What Rodriguez v Sprig Technologies Inc claims and in what amount.
Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming Ryan Glasgow.
gaps.noAction: Not required for a business deposit account where the business-level searches have run.

Collect a beneficial ownership certification naming every 25% owner and the control person, and stating whether Mixboard Inc. is a former name or a separate owner.
A Delaware corporation publishes no shareholders, and the San Francisco registration names Mixboard Inc. as owner of the Sprig name.

Run KYC on Ryan Glasgow.
He is the sole officer on the record and the likely signer, and no identity verification is held.

Disposition the adverse media items against Ryan Glasgow's and Richard Tatum's identifiers.
The theft report and the Columbus shooting and Fourth Circuit pension items match on name only and none references the business.

Confirm the physical operating address.
The submitted office address is a private mailbox; the California filing and current San Francisco registration list 71 Stevenson St Ste 600.

Ask the business for the claim, amount and status of Rodriguez v Sprig Technologies Inc.
The civil rights case is open in San Diego County with no amount on the record.

meroxa, inc..name: Bank account opening
meroxa, inc..brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to a beneficial ownership certification, KYC on Ali Hamidi and DeVaris Brown, and documented clearance of the watchlist and adverse media name matches.

body.text: MEROXA, INC. is a Delaware corporation, file 7665070, registered 21 October 2019, and the submitted name matches the filing. Delaware publishes no status for the domestic filing.

It holds two foreign registrations: California, file 4528561 (6 November 2019), active and in good standing at the submitted Oakland office address; and Utah, file 12039471-0143 (30 November 2020), inactive.

The website, meroxa.com, was not submitted; it shows the business name. Facebook and LinkedIn profiles were found, also unsubmitted. The filings name no officer, owner entity or registered agent beyond those submitted.

gaps.point: Good standing of the Delaware domestic filing.
gaps.noAction: Delaware publishes no status or sub-status; the California filing at the submitted address is active and in good standing.

body.text: The watchlist screen returned two name hits, both against Ali Hamidi: an OFAC SDN entry for ALI, Ahmed Mohammed Hamed (alias ALI, Hamed) and an INTERPOL Red Notice for Hamid Ali. Both share only the name Ali with him and neither carries the surname Hamidi, so the screen treats neither as a valid match. Nothing was returned on DeVaris Brown or the business.
The PEP screen found no hits on either submitted individual or their relatives and close associates.

Adverse media matched 19 negative items to Ali Hamidi, all Australian outlets covering one New South Wales corruption story: an ICAC finding against Samer Soliman, head of RMS, and a syndicated report that an NSW official gave $12m in deals to associates. They are tagged fraud, bribery and corruption with high confidence and money laundering with low to moderate confidence; the headlines name another person, and nothing ties the story to Ali Hamidi beyond the name.

Six negative items were matched to DeVaris Brown across two stories: the Twitter alternative Spill climbing the App Store charts, and former Twitter employees' unreturned work laptops, tagged cybercrime and fraud. No item names the business, and none was matched to MEROXA, INC. itself.

gaps.point: A documented disposition of the SDN and INTERPOL hits against Ali Hamidi's date of birth and nationality.
Whether any of the matched coverage concerns the submitted Ali Hamidi or DeVaris Brown rather than a namesake or a passing mention.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A reviewer disposition of each story against the individuals' KYC identifiers.

gaps.point: Criminal history of the submitted individuals; the check was not ordered.
gaps.noAction: Not required to open a business deposit account; its absence says nothing about the individuals.

body.text: The business classifies as a software publisher (NAICS 513210; MCC 7372, computer programming), outside high-risk and prohibited categories. The online website presents a low-code real-time data streaming platform and names a submitted person; the online Facebook profile, categorised as a software company, and LinkedIn page describe the same line of work. Software publishing is not a licensed activity, so no licence is expected.

The submitted office, 1111 Broadway Ste 300, Oakland, matches the California filing and is a deliverable commercial property, the business is active in California, and the website shows an address within 0.2 miles of it. Of the other submitted addresses, 2261 Market St #4146, San Francisco is a USPS commercial mail receiving agency and 24147 Amaranth Loop, Hayward is residential; both appear only on the inactive Utah filing.

Both submitted people are matched to the record. Ali Hamidi is chief executive, chief financial officer and secretary on the California filing and its registered agent; DeVaris Brown is director and president on the inactive Utah filing and its registered agent. The Delaware filing names only LEGALINC Corporate Services Inc., the submitted registered agent.
As a Delaware corporation, its shareholders appear in no filing, so beneficial owners at 25% or more rest on the customer's certification. No owning entity appears on the record.

Five connections were found. DeVaris Brown is also linked to DEVARIS BROWN CONSULTING, LLC, FLOODGATE ACADEMY INC. and CADERA BRANDS, INC. HIVEMIND PRINT AND DESIGN, LLC and LOTT CRAPSE HOLDINGS LLC share only the West Valley City, Utah residence given as the registered agent address on the inactive Utah filing, and no people.

gaps.point: Who holds 25% or more of the shares, and who exercises control.
Identity verification of Ali Hamidi and DeVaris Brown.

body.text: Tax and UCC lien, bankruptcy and litigation searches on the business returned nothing: no liens, no bankruptcy filings and no related litigation for a software company formed in 2019.

gaps.point: Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming Ali Hamidi or DeVaris Brown.
gaps.noAction: Not required to open a deposit account where the business-level record is clear.

followUps.text:
Collect a beneficial ownership certification naming each 25% owner and a control person, and confirming Ali Hamidi's and DeVaris Brown's roles.
No Delaware or foreign filing publishes the corporation's shareholders.

Run KYC on Ali Hamidi and DeVaris Brown.
Both are submitted officers and no identity verification is held.

Clear the OFAC SDN and INTERPOL Red Notice hits against Ali Hamidi's KYC date of birth and nationality, and record the disposition.
Both listed names share only Ali with him and neither carries Hamidi.

Disposition the adverse media matched to Ali Hamidi and DeVaris Brown against their KYC identifiers.
The NSW corruption coverage names another official, and the Twitter-related coverage is tied to DeVaris Brown by name only.
