alliance transfer inc..name: Bank account opening
alliance transfer inc..brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to confirming ALLIANCE ENTERPRISES IV, INC. as the applicant operating as Alliance Transfer, a beneficial ownership certification with KYC and screening of its owners and signers, a verified operating address, and evidence of household goods carrier authority.

body.text: The submitted name, Alliance Transfer Inc., is matched on the record, and the entity is a New York corporation whose name suffix matches its type. The one active domestic filing, however, is under a different legal name: ALLIANCE ENTERPRISES IV, INC., New York file 3538117, registered 29 June 2007, which also holds an active New York sales tax permit and a 2025 New Jersey foreign filing.

The two filings carrying the Alliance Transfer name, ALLIANCE TRANSFER (file 392025, 1976) and ALLIANCE TRANSFER CORP. (file 1920863, 1995), are both inactive. No assumed-name filing links the active corporation to the submitted name, which appears on the business's LinkedIn profile, a similar match to the submitted name.
No TIN, website, phone or people were submitted. The submitted office address is on none of the filings.

gaps.point: Whether ALLIANCE ENTERPRISES IV, INC. is the applicant, operating as Alliance Transfer, and so the legal name the account is opened in.
Whether ALLIANCE ENTERPRISES IV, INC. is in good standing: New York publishes an active status but no good-standing sub-status.

body.text: The watchlist screen returned no hits across the 14 lists searched, including OFAC's SDN and the Commerce Department's Entity and Denied Persons lists. The adverse media screen returned no results.

The PEP screen returned no hits, but it covers submitted individuals and none were submitted, so the officers named on the filings, Richard Kawas and Michael Kawas, have not been screened as individuals.

gaps.point: PEP and adverse media screening of the business's owners and signers once they are identified.
Criminal history of the business's principals; the check was not ordered.
gaps.noAction: Not a standard requirement for opening a business deposit account.

body.text: The business classifies as a household and office goods mover (NAICS 484210), with packing, crating and general warehousing as secondary codes, all outside the prohibited and restricted industry categories. No website was found; an online LinkedIn company profile under the Alliance Transfer name is the only web presence.

The submitted office address, 503 5th Ave, New York, is a commercial property that matches no filing, is undeliverable by USPS, and differs from the address found on the web. The filings instead place the business at 140 58th St, Brooklyn, a commercial address on the active filing and the sales tax permit, with a further commercial address in Newark, New Jersey. The business is active in New York, the state of the submitted address.

Household goods moving is regulated activity: interstate moves require USDOT registration and FMCSA operating authority, and intrastate moves in New York require New York State Department of Transportation household goods carrier authority.

gaps.point: Whether the business holds USDOT registration, FMCSA household goods authority and NYSDOT intrastate authority in its own legal name.
gaps.wouldAnswer: An FMCSA SAFER / Licensing and Insurance lookup and a NYSDOT household goods carrier lookup for ALLIANCE ENTERPRISES IV, INC.

body.text: No owners or signers were submitted and none is verified. The active filing names Richard Kawas as an officer; Michael Kawas appears as CEO and as the registered agent on the New Jersey foreign filing; Denise Pulice is named only on the inactive 1995 Alliance Transfer Corp. filing. New York corporate filings publish no shareholders, and no business entity is named as an owner, so the ownership structure is not on the record.

Eleven connections were found, all through the two Kawas officers or shared filing addresses. Richard C. Kawas links the business to Metropolitan Relocations, Inc. and Metropolitan Relocation Services, Inc., both through the residential Little Silver, New Jersey address on the active filing and both in the same line of work, and to Installation Plus Svs. Corp. Michael Kawas links it to five others, including Next Generation Industry Leaders Inc. at the New Jersey registered-agent address. MRKAYE Realty, Miraga Realty and RVL Properties share filing addresses only.

gaps.point: Who owns the corporation, their percentages, and who controls it and will sign.
Identity verification of the owners and signers.
Whether Metropolitan Relocations, Inc. and Metropolitan Relocation Services, Inc. are affiliates under common ownership.

body.text: Two UCC filings against ALLIANCE ENTERPRISES IV, INC. are open, both all-assets: Live Oak Banking Company (June 2025), securing an SBA-program loan, and TD Bank (August 2019), whose collateral includes deposit accounts. Six earlier filings, including SBA, equipment-lease and bank filings dating to 2009, are closed. Secured bank and SBA credit is ordinary for an operating moving and storage business.

Two cases name the business as defendant: a 2007 Kings County Civil Court suit by Brooklyn Union Gas against Alliance Transfer Corp., closed, and a 2015 Eastern District of New York employee-benefit action by United Benefit Fund against Alliance Enterprises IV, Inc., status unknown. Neither carries a money judgment on the record. There are no bankruptcy filings.

gaps.point: The outcome of the 2015 United Benefit Fund action (1:15-cv-03402).
gaps.noAction: Filed eleven years ago with no judgment on the record; not material to opening a deposit account.

gaps.point: Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the business's principals.
gaps.noAction: Not required to open a deposit account where the business-level record is available.

followUps.text:
Confirm the applicant is ALLIANCE ENTERPRISES IV, INC. (NY file 3538117) and collect its assumed-name certificate for Alliance Transfer.
The only active filing is under that name; both Alliance Transfer filings are inactive.

Collect a beneficial ownership certification naming each 25% owner, the control person and the authorized signers, including the roles of Richard Kawas and Michael Kawas.
No people were submitted and New York publishes no shareholders.

Run KYC, PEP and adverse media screening on each certified owner and signer.
The PEP screen covered submitted individuals only, and none were submitted.

Obtain proof of the operating address.
The submitted 503 5th Ave address matches no filing and is undeliverable; the filings place the business at 140 58th St, Brooklyn.

Verify USDOT/FMCSA household goods authority and NYSDOT intrastate authority in the corporation's name.
Moving is licensed activity and no check on the record covers it.

Submit an RFI for a Certificate of Good Standing for ALLIANCE ENTERPRISES IV, INC.
New York publishes an active status but no good-standing sub-status.

Ask whether Metropolitan Relocations, Inc. and Metropolitan Relocation Services, Inc. are affiliates under common ownership.
Both connect through Richard C. Kawas and the Little Silver address, in the same line of work.

checkr, inc..name: Bank account opening
checkr, inc..brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to a beneficial ownership certification through the ownership chain, KYC on the control person and signers, disposition of the adverse media item on Jennifer Yeh, and evidence the Florida tax lien is released.

body.text: CHECKR, INC. is a Delaware corporation, formed 24 March 2014 (file 5503562), and the submitted name matches the state filings. It holds active foreign qualifications in 19 states, including California, where the submitted San Francisco office sits. Its website, checkr.com, carries the same name.

The one inactive filing is a Utah record (12328450-0142, expired) that the source labels domestic. Utah also carries an active foreign qualification registered the same day under the adjacent file number, 12328450-0143, so the Delaware filing remains the formation of record.

gaps.point: Whether the Delaware corporation is in good standing.
gaps.noAction: Delaware publishes no filing status; this is normal for a Delaware corporation and not a finding.

body.text: The watchlist screen returned no hits across the 14 lists searched, including OFAC SDN, Sectoral Sanctions and the BIS Entity List. The PEP screen returned no hits on the submitted individuals or their relatives and close associates.

Adverse media returned items against four people. Ten items are matched to Daniel Yanisse, eight of them tagged fraud and cybercrime; their headlines report the company's acquisition of Truv and its pursuit of government contracts to reduce benefit fraud, not an allegation against the business or Mr Yanisse. One item matched to Jennifer Yeh, a USA Herald report of FEMA seeking dismissal of an attorney's bias suit tagged fraud and corruption, has nothing on the record tying it to this Jennifer Yeh beyond the name.

The remaining items carry no risk tags: a podcast naming Naeem Ishaq as Checkr's CFO, and a stock-sale report on a Wag! group COO named Dylan Allread, who appears on this record only through a Form 5500 filing.

gaps.point: Whether the FEMA bias-suit article concerns the submitted Jennifer Yeh or a namesake.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A reviewer disposition of the article against Jennifer Yeh's KYC identifiers.

gaps.point: Criminal history of the submitted officers.
gaps.noAction: Not ordered and not standard for a business deposit account; the watchlist and PEP screens are clear.

body.text: The business classifies as a credit bureau (NAICS 561450), with custom software and credit reporting agency codes alongside, none of them high-risk or prohibited. The website presents a background check and verification platform, and nine online third-party profiles, including two BBB listings categorised as employment background checks, describe the same line of work.

The submitted office, 1 Montgomery St Ste 2400, San Francisco, matches the filings, is a deliverable commercial property, and appears on the website, which also names a submitted officer; the business is active in California. The submitted Midvale, Utah address is a registered-agent address that also sits on the expired Utah filing.
As a consumer reporting business, its activity is regulated, and some states license or register background screening firms.

gaps.point: Whether the business holds the state licences or registrations its background screening activity requires where it operates.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A state licensing lookup for consumer reporting and background screening in the states where it is qualified.

body.text: The three submitted people match the state filings: Daniel Yanisse as CEO, President and Director, Jennifer Yeh as Secretary and Naeem Ishaq as Treasurer. The filings also name Tim Yarbrough as CFO and Treasurer and Todd Freedman as Treasurer, neither submitted. C T Corporation System appears only for service of process, as registered agent, not as an officer.

As a corporation, its filings publish officers but no shareholders. The 14 connections point to a group: CHECKR GROUP, INC. shares all five officers and the Delaware and San Francisco addresses, and Tessera Data, Zethos, Inflection.com, Inflection Risk Solutions and Checkr.org share officers and addresses. The rest connect through a single officer's other affiliations.

gaps.point: Who owns 25% or more of the corporation, and whether CHECKR GROUP, INC. sits above it in the ownership chain.
Identity verification of the control person and authorised signers.

body.text: One state tax lien is on record: the State of Florida, $3,619.82, filed 11 December 2024 (J24000777456), status not reported. One UCC filing is open, in Delaware, filed 18 December 2024 by JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. as collateral agent, with no collateral stated. Filings by Hercules Capital as agent and two by the California Employment Development Department are closed.

Ten open cases name the business, all filed in August and September 2026, with the business as defendant or real party in interest and no judgments. Most are individual consumer credit and commercial claims, including three by Roger Barone and a duplicated Puskas docket in New Jersey, which is consistent with a background screening business. There are no bankruptcy filings.

gaps.point: Whether the Florida state tax lien has been paid or released.
What the open JPMorgan Chase collateral filing secures, and whether it reaches deposit accounts.
Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted officers.
gaps.noAction: Not required to open a deposit account where the business-level record is on file.

followUps.text:
Collect a beneficial ownership certification naming every 25% owner and the control person, tracing through CHECKR GROUP, INC. if it is the parent.
The filings publish officers but no shareholders, and CHECKR GROUP, INC. shares all five officers and the Delaware address.

Run KYC on the control person and each authorised signer, and confirm the current CFO.
No identity verification is held, and the filings name both Naeem Ishaq and Tim Yarbrough in the finance role.

Disposition the FEMA bias-suit article matched to Jennifer Yeh against her KYC identifiers.
It is tagged fraud and corruption and matched on name only.

Request evidence that the Florida state tax lien of $3,619.82 is paid or released.
It was filed in December 2024 and the record reports no status.

Confirm what the open JPMorgan Chase collateral filing secures and whether the credit agreement requires control over deposit accounts.
The Delaware UCC filing is open and states no collateral.

Confirm the business holds any state licence or registration required for background screening where it operates.
It classifies as a credit reporting business and no check on the record covers licensing.

zendesk, inc..name: Bank account opening
zendesk, inc..brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to clearing the adverse media matched to five officers and directors, a beneficial ownership certification, evidence of signing authority with KYC on the signers, and tax lien release evidence.

body.text: The submitted name matches the Delaware domestic filing for ZENDESK, INC., a corporation incorporated on 3 March 2009 (file 4661237), with RL&F Service Corp. as registered agent. Delaware publishes no filing status or sub-status.

Of 51 filings, 36 are active, including the California foreign filing for the state of the submitted office address; 15 foreign filings carry a good-standing sub-status. The two without a status are Delaware and New Jersey, which publish none.

Thirteen filings are inactive. Eight are superseded by an active filing in the same state (Florida, two in Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Tennessee, Utah, Virginia, Wisconsin); Georgia and Illinois were withdrawn, Louisiana is inactive, Missouri was administratively dissolved and Oklahoma reads "Ousted".
The website, zendesk.com, was not submitted; it shows the submitted business name. No TIN or phone was submitted, so neither was checked.

Watchlist screening returned no hits for the business or any screened person across the 14 OFAC, BIS and State Department lists. PEP screening returned no hits on the submitted individuals or their relatives and close associates.

Adverse media returned no articles for the business name or for Tom Eggemeier, and nothing for Caryn Marooney. Julie Swinney's three articles report her appointment as CFO, and John Geschke's two report his sales of Zendesk shares; none is negative.

Negative articles attach to three directors named alongside the prior board on the active Utah, Nevada and New Mexico filings, and to Peter Fenton, named on an inactive Virginia filing. Michael Curtis: 17 syndicated reports of a police investigation into an HOA manager who may have scammed people of $1 million, tagged fraud. Michelle Wilson: one UK court listing, criminal case SCS/2026-015600, for a Michelle Wilson, tagged fraud and weapons. Michael Frandsen: two Dayton Daily News pieces on nonprofit and private-school executive pay. Peter Fenton: 20 copies of a law-firm notice of a class action by purchasers of Zuora, Inc. stock.

Shana Simmons, a submitted officer, returned two negative articles on cyberattacks on other organisations (a Bloomberg Law piece on cloud data-privacy liability and one on the New York City Law Department). Elena Gomez, a former CFO, returned 18 articles mostly about namesakes, including murder and car-crash reports, alongside items on a Zendesk CFO share sale. None of these articles names ZENDESK, INC. as a party, and nothing on the record ties any of them to these people beyond the name.
"WITHDRAWN" and "NOT YET ELECTED", placeholder text in the officer fields of the Illinois and Michigan filings, were screened as names and returned 42 unrelated articles.

gaps.point: Whether the fraud and criminal-case articles matched to Michael Curtis, Michelle Wilson, Michael Frandsen and Peter Fenton, and the cyberattack articles matched to Shana Simmons, concern these individuals or namesakes.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A reviewer disposition of each article against the individual's identifiers (date of birth, residence, role) and current board status.

gaps.point: Criminal history on the officers has not been searched.
gaps.noAction: Not part of account-opening screening for officers of an operating corporation; sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening cover the obligation.

body.text: Industry classification places the business in software publishing (NAICS 513210) and custom computer programming (NAICS 541511).

The website, online when the record was ordered, presents a customer service software platform, and the four third-party profiles (Trustpilot, BBB, TikTok, Google), all online, list it as a software company. Software publishing requires no activity licence; the business holds active city registrations in San Francisco and in Seattle, the latter for custom computer programming services.

The submitted office address, 181 Fremont St Fl 17, San Francisco, matches the filings, is a deliverable commercial property and is shown on the website, and the business is active in California. The website names people other than the submitted officers.
ZENDESK, INC. is a Delaware corporation, and Delaware publishes no shareholders; the domestic filing names only its registered agent. Beneficial ownership rests on what the business certifies.

The filings name all three submitted people: Tom Eggemeier as CEO and President, Julie Swinney as CFO and Treasurer, and Shana Simmons as Director and Secretary, including on an August 2026 Virginia filing. Active filings in Utah, Nevada, New Mexico, West Virginia and New York still name Mikkel Svane, the first four with Hasani Caraway and a prior board.

The connections run through current and former officers and directors who sit on other companies' filings, and through shared registered-agent addresses; Zendesk Neighbor Foundation also shares the submitted address. None is named as an owner or parent of the business.

gaps.point: Who holds 25% or more of the company, if anyone, and who is its control person.
Who is authorised to open and sign on the account; filings name officers, not signers, and five active filings still name Mikkel Svane.
Identity verification of the signers and certified owners has not been run.

body.text: Four state tax liens are on file: New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration (September 2024, open), two State of Utah liens (May 2022 and May 2025) and one State of Mississippi lien (February 2022), the last three with no published status. None carries an amount.

Three UCC filings are open: a 2025 California filing for Mitsubishi HC Capital America and PaymentWorks Acquisition Company covering receivables sold to them; a 2022 Delaware filing for Blue Owl Capital Corporation and Owl Rock Capital Corporation as agent, with no collateral described; and a 2011 Delaware filing for Dell Financial Services that lapses in December 2026. Three older filings, to The Swenson Group and Silicon Valley Bank, are closed.

Eight litigations name the business, with no money judgment in any. It is a defendant in an open employment discrimination suit and a wrongful termination suit of unknown status, co-defendant with Discord, Inc. in two open suits, and was defendant in three closed patent and civil rights cases; it is plaintiff in an open commercial suit against Enchanted Fairies Studio LLC. There are no bankruptcy filings.

gaps.point: The amounts of the four state tax liens and whether each is paid or released.
What the Blue Owl / Owl Rock agented filing secures, and whether deposit accounts are among the collateral.
Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted officers have not been searched.
gaps.noAction: The account is the corporation's; officers' personal records do not bear on its obligations.

followUps.text:
Disposition the adverse media matched to Michael Curtis, Michelle Wilson, Michael Frandsen, Peter Fenton and Shana Simmons against each person's identifiers and current role.
The articles cover an HOA fraud investigation, a UK criminal case, executive-pay reporting, a securities class action and cyberattacks, and none names the business.

Obtain a beneficial ownership certification naming any 25% owner and the control person.
Delaware publishes no shareholders.

Obtain a board resolution or incumbency certificate naming the authorised signers.
Filings name officers, not signers, and five active filings still name Mikkel Svane.

Run KYC on each authorised signer and certified owner.
No identity verification has been run.

Request payoff or release evidence for the New Hampshire, Utah and Mississippi state tax liens.
The filings carry no amounts, and three have no published status.

Ask what the Blue Owl / Owl Rock agented facility secures and whether it requires control over deposit accounts.
The 2022 filing is open and describes no collateral.

liens.collateral: EXHIBIT A TO UCC-1 FINANCING STATEMENT All of Debtor's right, title and interest in, to and under, whether now existing or hereafter acquired and wheresoever located: all purchased Receivables purchased by PWAC from Debtor, including as purchased under the EPT, and all other rights of Debtor and obligations of Customer with respect to each Receivable, including all Related Security, and all cash, checks, money orders and other items of value, including all funds that are received by or on behalf of Debtor in payment of any amounts owed thereon (including purchase price, finance charges, interest and all other charges), or applied to amounts owed thereon (including insurance payments and net proceeds of disposition of repossessed goods or other collateral or property of the related Customer or any other Person liable for payment thereon and available to be applied thereon), now or hereafter paid, deposited, credited or held in the Lockbox, and all proceeds or products of all of the foregoing (collectively, "Assets"). A list of the accounts purchased by PWAC under the EPT is available from PWAC at the address set forth above. PWAC HAS PURCHASED (OR WILL PURCHASE) ACCOUNTS OF DEBTOR AND ALL PROCEEDS THEREOF, AND DEBTOR AND PWAC INTEND THAT PWAC, SUBJECT TO FURTHER RESALE BY PWAC TO MHCA, IS THE SOLE AND EXCLUSIVE OWNER THEREOF. THIS FILING SHOULD NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A CONCLUSION THAT PWAC, AND SUBSEQUENTLY MHCA, DOES NOT OWN ACCOUNTS AND PROCEEDS. Notwithstanding the foregoing, "Assets" shall not at any time include or be deemed to include in any manner whatsoever any Assets which are repurchased by Debtor pursuant to the terms of the EPT for any reason (the "Repurchased Assets") and the collateral expressly excludes the Repurchased Assets. Definitions "Receivable(s)" means an account that relates to Debtor's right to receive payment from a Customer resulting from a business relationship between such Customer and Debtor and meets the eligibility criteria under the EPT. "Customer" means a customer of PaymentWorks, Inc. meeting PWAC's underwriting/eligibility requirements that purchases goods or services from Debtor and that has entered into an agreement with PaymentWorks, Inc. relating to the PaymentWorks EarlyPay Program. A Customer is an account debtor under the UCC. "EPT" means the EarlyPay Terms of Service, to which Debtor and PWAC are a party, as amended, restated or otherwise modified or supplemented from time to time. "Lockbox" means the deposit account held by PWAC or its affiliate, or MHCA, to collect payments associated with Receivables purchased by PWAC. "Person" means an individual, business (in any form), government agency, or political subdivision. "Related Security" means, with respect to any purchased Receivable, as applicable: (i) all of Debtor's interest in all credits from vendors upon the return to, recall or repurchase by such vendor; (ii) all books and records relating to, and all instruments and chattel paper that may evidence, such Receivable; (iii) all other security interests or liens and property subject thereto from time to time purporting to secure payment of such Receivable, whether pursuant to the contract related to such Receivable or otherwise, together with all UCC financing statements or similar filings relating thereto; (iv) all of Debtor's rights, interests and claims under the related contracts and all guaranties, letters of credit, indemnities, insurance (including any credit insurance) and other agreements or arrangements supporting or securing payment of such Receivable, or otherwise relating thereto; and (v) all proceeds and products of any of the foregoing.

userleap inc.name: Bank account opening
userleap inc.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to opening the account in the legal name Mixboard Inc., a beneficial ownership certification with KYC on Ryan Glasgow and the adverse media item cleared, and evidence of California registration.

body.text: Userleap INC holds no Secretary of State filing under the submitted name. It is a trade name: the San Francisco business registration lists Userleap Inc. as a DBA of Mixboard Inc., and the Userleap location on that registration ran from November 2017 to August 2021.

The legal entity is MIXBOARD INC., a Delaware corporation (file 6473823). The linked Mixboard Inc. record shares three San Francisco addresses with this one, including the submitted 1759 Chestnut St address, and names Ryan Glasgow, the submitted person.
The website found, sprig.com, presents the business as Sprig rather than under the submitted name; the same San Francisco registration lists Sprig Technologies Inc as a current DBA of Mixboard Inc.

gaps.point: Good standing of MIXBOARD INC.: Delaware publishes no registration status.
gaps.noAction: Delaware publishes no status for any entity; this is normal and not a finding.

body.text: The watchlist screen returned no hits across the OFAC, BIS and State Department lists. The PEP screen returned no hits on Ryan Glasgow or his relatives and close associates.

The adverse media screen matched one negative article to Ryan Glasgow and none to the business: a Guyana Times report of a man jailed for two years over the theft of a brush cutter, tagged fraud, bribery and corruption. The match rests on the name alone, and nothing on the record ties the article to the submitted Ryan Glasgow.

gaps.point: Whether the Guyana Times theft article concerns the submitted Ryan Glasgow or a namesake.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A reviewer disposition of the article against the signer's KYC identifiers (date of birth, residential address).

gaps.point: Criminal history on Ryan Glasgow was not ordered.
gaps.noAction: Not a standard account-opening check; the watchlist, PEP and adverse media screens cover the screening obligation.

body.text: The business classifies as custom computer programming (NAICS 541511) and marketing research (NAICS 541910); the industry screen found no prohibited or restricted classification. The website found, sprig.com, is online, presents an enterprise research software platform and names Ryan Glasgow; the one third-party profile, on Trustpilot, is online and categorised as a software company. Software of this kind requires no industry licence.

The submitted office address, 1759 Chestnut St # C, San Francisco, is matched to the business and deliverable, and is a residential property; the website shows a different address. The business is not registered in California, the state of that address, and the record holds only the Delaware domestic filing for Mixboard Inc.

gaps.point: Whether Mixboard Inc. is registered to do business in California, where it operates.

body.text: Ryan Glasgow, the only person submitted, is not matched to a filing under the submitted name, which has none; he is named on the linked Mixboard Inc. record without a title. The Delaware filing publishes no officers or shareholders, so the record establishes neither his role nor who owns the corporation.
The structure on the record is one corporation trading under a DBA. No business connections were found.

gaps.point: Who owns Mixboard Inc., in what percentages, and Ryan Glasgow's role and authority to sign.
Identity verification of Ryan Glasgow.

body.text: Tax and UCC lien, bankruptcy and litigation searches returned nothing on the business.

gaps.point: Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming Ryan Glasgow were not ordered.
gaps.noAction: Not required to open a deposit account where the business-level record is clear.

followUps.text:
Open the account in the legal name Mixboard Inc., with its Delaware certificate of incorporation, and confirm whether Userleap is still a trade name in use.
Userleap INC has no state filing; it is a San Francisco DBA of Mixboard Inc. whose location closed in August 2021, and the website trades as Sprig.

Collect a beneficial ownership certification for Mixboard Inc. naming each owner, their percentage and Ryan Glasgow's role and signing authority.
Delaware publishes no officers or shareholders, and Ryan Glasgow is named on the linked record without a title.

Run KYC on Ryan Glasgow.
He is the only person submitted and no identity verification is held.

Clear the adverse media item against Ryan Glasgow's KYC identifiers.
One Guyana Times article on a man jailed for theft is matched to his name only.

Obtain evidence that Mixboard Inc. is registered to do business in California.
It operates from San Francisco, and the record holds only its Delaware domestic filing.

Confirm the current operating address.
The submitted address is residential and the website shows a different one.

mixboard inc..name: Bank account opening
mixboard inc..brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to a beneficial ownership certification, KYC on Ryan Glasgow with the adverse media item cleared, evidence of his signing authority, and confirmation of California qualification.

body.text: The submitted name matches the Delaware domestic filing for MIXBOARD INC., a corporation incorporated on 10 July 2017 (file 6473823), with The Company Corporation as registered agent at 251 Little Falls Dr, Wilmington. Delaware publishes no filing status or sub-status, so the filing carries none.

San Francisco business registrations under account 1080965, owned by Mixboard Inc. since November 2017, carry two further names: Userleap Inc. and Sprig Technologies Inc. The Sprig Technologies DBA is open at the submitted Chestnut Street address and, since October 2024, at 71 Stevenson St Ste 600.
Watchlist screening returned no hits across the 14 OFAC, BIS and State Department lists searched. PEP screening returned no hits on Ryan Glasgow or his relatives and close associates.

Adverse media screening returned nothing on the business name. It holds one negative item matched to Ryan Glasgow at an 87% match score: a Guyana Times report of a two-year jail sentence for theft, tagged fraud, bribery and corruption. Nothing on the record ties the article to this Ryan Glasgow beyond the name.

gaps.point: Whether the Guyana Times article concerns the submitted Ryan Glasgow or a namesake.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A reviewer disposition of the article against Ryan Glasgow's KYC identifiers (date of birth, residential address).

gaps.point: Screening covers only Ryan Glasgow; beneficial owners and signers not yet disclosed have not been screened.
Criminal history on Ryan Glasgow was not ordered.
gaps.noAction: Not a standard requirement to open a deposit account; the one adverse media item is dispositioned separately.

body.text: Industry classification places the business in custom computer programming (NAICS 541511) and software publishing (NAICS 513210), neither of them a prohibited or restricted industry. Software development carries no activity licence requirement.

No website was found for the business; the only third-party profile is an online Instagram account under the Mixboard name with five followers. What the business sells and to whom rests on the classification alone.

The submitted office address, 1759 Chestnut St #C, San Francisco, is matched to the business and deliverable, and is a residential property. The corporation is not registered in California, the state of that address.

gaps.point: What the business sells, to whom, and the account activity it expects.
gaps.wouldAnswer: The business's website and a customer-supplied description of its product, customers and expected account activity.

gaps.point: Whether the business operates from the residential Chestnut Street address or 71 Stevenson St Ste 600.

body.text: MIXBOARD INC. is a Delaware corporation, and Delaware publishes neither shareholders nor officers; the filing names none. Ownership and control rest on what the business certifies.
The submitted person, Ryan Glasgow, is not matched to any filing and no title was submitted for him. No connected businesses were found, so the record shows no parent or affiliated entity.

gaps.point: Who holds 25% or more of the corporation, and who controls it.
Ryan Glasgow's office and authority to sign for the corporation.
Identity verification of Ryan Glasgow has not been run.

body.text: No tax or UCC liens, litigation or bankruptcy filings were found against the business, nine years after incorporation.

gaps.point: Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming Ryan Glasgow have not been searched.
gaps.noAction: Not required to open a deposit account where the business-level record is clear.

followUps.text:
Obtain a beneficial ownership certification naming each 25% owner and the control person.
Delaware publishes no shareholders or officers, so nothing on the record identifies them.

Run KYC and screening on Ryan Glasgow and each certified owner.
Only Ryan Glasgow has been screened, and no one has been identity-verified.

Clear the adverse media item against Ryan Glasgow's KYC identifiers.
One negative Guyana Times article on a theft conviction is matched to his name only.

Obtain an incumbency certificate or board resolution showing Ryan Glasgow's office and authority to sign.
No filing names him and no title was submitted.

Request evidence of California foreign qualification, or why it is not required.
The business operates from San Francisco and is not registered in California.

Confirm the principal place of business.
The submitted address is residential, while the active Sprig Technologies DBA also lists 71 Stevenson St Ste 600.

Request the business website and a description of its product, customers and expected account activity.
No website was found to corroborate what it does.

reviews.text:
Over the summer, my father, my husband and I decided to build our own backyard fence. We knew this would be a huge project and we were intimidated to say the least but the professionals at Expert Fence couldn't have been more helpful.

From start to finish, Samuel helped us with what materials to buy, how much and even gave detailed instructions on how to complete every step. It felt like we had a million questions for him but he was incredibly patient and explained the process every step of the way, even going so far as to draw us diagrams.

It took us two months, but we are very proud of the fence we built! We couldn't have done it without the guidance of Expert Fence. Thanks so much for all of your help!

I signed a contract with this company on May 21 for a fence installation project totaling over $14,000. It is now three months later and the fence still isn't installed.

The permit application wasn't even filed until July 9 — nearly seven weeks after I signed. DDOT sent back comments requiring correction on July 30, and I still have no confirmation on whether those were ever addressed. At every step, I've had to be the one reaching out for updates — nothing has been proactive.

For a project of this size, I expected regular communication and a clear timeline. Instead I've gotten silence and delays with no explanation. If you're considering this company, be prepared to manage the project yourself, because they won't keep you informed.
Efficient. Quick to fix a little problem that came up after installation.

I’m a landscape contractor, and Expert Fence is our trusted partner for all of our fencing projects. They consistently deliver outstanding results and have never let me down.

Samuel Lazo is extremely knowledgeable, communicative, and professional throughout every project. The quality of the finished work and the satisfaction of our shared clients speak for themselves.

I highly recommend that anyone in the DMV considering a fencing project give Samuel and the Expert Fence team a call.

May 7, 2026
Expert Fence installed my Georgetown fence and metal mesh a few months ago. I needed a warped post replaced. Jose and Luis arrived punctually for the replacement and took the time to explain the process and showed me the material to be used. They were polite and bilingual. Great job!!!

For anyone looking to get a new fence, this is an important thing to consider: Expert Fence installed a beautiful fence for us 5 years ago. We discovered an issue this past week because of the clay soil, and I was worried about high costs of getting a resolution. The team, led by Mr. Sammy, took care of the issue today. Obviously, there is no such thing as a warranty 5 years later, but they value their customers and they took care of issue because that is the right thing to do.
Expert Fence installed a horizontal 6 foot privacy fence, trash enclose, and gate. We couldn't be more pleased with the quality of work and attention to detail.

Expert Fence has installed dozens of custom fence and gate designs for me and my clients, and they always do a beautiful job. Their prices are fair for the materials and work involved, and they are very good about making sure everything is completed to the highest standards. Great company!
Expert Fence does excellent work, on time and on budget.

Fantastic Workmanship!

We recently had a new fence installed by Expert Fence of Alexandria. Can’t tell how pleased we are! The foreman, Jose, came out and conducted an estimate and provided expert advice on the best choice for our property, recommended the optimal wood, and suggested hardware. We took him up on his approach and scheduled an appointment. The team arrived, headed up by another excellent craftsman, also named Jose. They were on time and came with all materials required. They carefully demo’ed and removed our old fence, sparing our shrubs and garden without any damage. The new fence was expertly erected and looked great. They cleaned up and left the property in perfect shape. But wait - there’s more! After the first rainstorm, there appeared a mold-like stain on the gate. Don’t know how or why? I took a couple of photos with my phone and emailed them to Expert Fence. Jose called me and we talked. Neither of us knew why the stain appeared but he offered to send the team out to look at it. Team leader Jose came this morning alone in the truck with all of the tools and materials to rebuild and replace the gate! Working alone, he rebuilt and rehung the gate and again, it looks perfect! Really professional workmanship! Thank you, Expert Fence, for your commitment to quality and customer service!

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED WITHOUT ANY RESERVATION! FIRST CLASS!

Mike Waschull
Alexandria, VA

recent_reviews.author: James S.

recent_reviews.text: I signed a contract on 8/2/21 to install a metal fence around our front yard in 3 months. In early November, I telephoned the office and was told that the materials had not yet arrived and that it would be another 2 months before the fence would be installed. In early January 2022, I telephoned the office again and arrangements were made to install the fence on January 12. The 4-man crew arrived about 7:30 a.m. and finished about 5 p.m. During the course of their work, the laborers cut 2 underground private electric lines. The foreman admitted that they had cut the lines accidently. They also left mud all over the driveway and sidewalks which I hosed down with water to wash the mud away after they left. I telephoned the office and said that I would not pay the balance due until the severed electric lines were fixed. The secretary pointed out to me that the estimate which I signed specifically stated: "Expert Fence shall not be liable for private underground utilities."  So, we agreed to pay the balance due and we will not hire the company again when we replace the back yard fence. My warning to readers of this post is to be sure to read the very fine print!
recent_reviews.author: Joseph S.

recent_reviews.text: The best fence company in Northern Virginia. Had a front and backyard fence put in by them and the process was so easy. Everyone in the office is awesome and the salesman and installers are great and very good at what they do. I would recommend them anytime of you need a professional fence company that does awesome work.
recent_reviews.author: Jennien J.

recent_reviews.text: I don't know what happened it it seems like this company has gone downhill recently. They installed a six foot high stockade fence for me 10 years ago and did a decent job.  Two years ago I asked that they replace two post - at my expense of course - and they did except the post are 4" shorter than all the others.  I've called them back about replacing some panels and they never call back.
recent_reviews.author: Robert M.

recent_reviews.text: I was just threatened by the owner of Expert Fence because I deducted a small amount from my invoice for work they didn't do and I had to pay others to do.  He said it was my responsibility to make sure they did what they were supposed to do, as opposed to the estimator communicating to the men who did the work, which boards to replace in my fence.  I was disappointed initially when my painter told me there were still rotten boards, but now I am furious.
recent_reviews.author: B H.

recent_reviews.text: I first called Expert Fence on August 7th to request an estimate on replacing my 32 year old dilapidated fence.  I was told that someone would be buy on August 13 @ 11 AM and the it was not necessary for me to be on-site.  I don't know if anyone ever showed up but I followed up 3 times to ask when I can expect to receive my estimate and all 3 times I was promised that Jose was working on it and I should have it shortly.  It is now August 21st and I get it...  They're not interested.  But I'm sure that if I had told them that me and 6 of my neighbors were looking to replace our fences they probably would have at least given me the courtesy of a call back or perhaps even a reasonable estimate.  That's unfortunate...  :-(
recent_reviews.author: Mercedes R.

recent_reviews.text: We met with Chris for an estimate and he couldn't have been nicer.  Unfortunately it's three weeks later and I still haven't received an estimate.  I called the office twice asking for an update, and no response.  If they are unable to take the job, or don't want it, just let me know.  That is better than radio silence.
recent_reviews.author: Devon C.

recent_reviews.text:
This review is long overdue: I had Expert Fence remove an old chain link fence and install a privacy fence on our small urban lot back in 2016. At the time there was a tree in the fence line and Expert Fence expertly installed a fence right up to the contours of the tree (with a little room to spare). But when in 2017 that tree came down, I had Expert Fence come back, remove the existing panels (for grinding the tree stump), and install a new post and panels to match the rest of the fence. Finally, just this week in 2019, when a gate post warped so much that the gate slammed shut and the mechanism wouldn't latch, I had Expert Fence come and put things back in order. So, to be clear, I've had several experiences with Expert Fence.

Each and every experience with Expert Fence has been great. On the original install I asked for cedar boards and stainless steel nails, which they delivered on, and I don't have any streaking on my fence. I also had a 16 foot wide car gate installed: Jose engineered a structure using steel 6x6 posts, steel frames, and a header to keep the gates from sagging, and to this day they are working perfectly. I've had several neighbors ask who did my fence and I proudly display the Expert Fence sign. For followup needs, it's easy to get a hold of the office, schedule a visit, and have the work done. Their team is great and clearly know what they're doing. The craftsmanship is top notch and I recommend the company to everyone with fence needs. I see no reason to look for another company: call Expert Fence.
recent_reviews.author: Joseph L.

recent_reviews.text: I do most work around the house myself and I am particular about attention to detail and craftsmanship--for which I am willing to pay.  I am often disappointed that I pay craftsmanship prices for amateur work.  This was NOT the case with Expert Fence.  They recently installed a cedar fence with gates and arbors for me.  I was very particular and even took the time to provide a detailed line drawing of what I wanted.  The workers paid particular attention to angles and fit which resulted in an extremely tight and neat finish to the work.  Their pride in their work really showed and was worth every penny I paid.
recent_reviews.author: Robert W.

recent_reviews.text: Kris and his fence did a fantastic job replacing our fence and adding additional pieces! His team completed our cedar fence in one day, and we're very patient with my wife's questions. We had a 4th of July incident where our fence was damaged, and he came out the same week to replace the piece at no cost to us. We enjoy the privacy we have now and love the work that Expert Fence did!
recent_reviews.author: Jayson W.

bradley reeves insurance agency inc.name: Bank account opening
bradley reeves insurance agency inc.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to reinstatement of the inactive Arkansas filing, IRS confirmation of the TIN, a beneficial ownership certification, disposition of the adverse media hit and evidence of the agency's insurance licence.

body.text: BRADLEY REEVES INSURANCE AGENCY INC is a distinct entity on the record: the submitted name matches an Arkansas domestic filing, the filing carries the entity type Corporation, and the name's suffix agrees with it. The domestic filing is inactive, and no active Secretary of State filing was found in any state. Arkansas does not publish a good-standing sub-status, so the filing's status is known only as inactive.

The IRS has no record for the submitted TIN and business name combination, so the TIN is not tied to the entity on the record. No website was found for the business, so no business name could be read from one; no phone or DBA was submitted and neither is assessed.

gaps.point: Whether the Arkansas corporation can be brought to good standing, since the state publishes no sub-status and the filing is inactive.

body.text: Sanctions and watchlist screening of the business returned no hits, and PEP screening returned no hits on submitted individuals or their relatives and close associates. Adverse media screening returned a hit, which has not been disposed of on the record.
No people were submitted on the application, so the people screenings rest on the individuals found on the filing rather than on named signers or owners, and no criminal history search was run.

The business is classified as Insurance Agencies and Brokerages, which is not a high-risk or prohibited industry. Insurance agencies are licensed activity in the state they sell in, and no licence check is on the record for this business or the people on its filing.

The submitted office address is a deliverable residential property that is a similar match to the address on the filing, and the business is inactive in that state. No website URL and no third-party profiles were found, so the submitted address could not be confirmed from a web source and there is no independent evidence of the business operating as an insurance agency.

gaps.point: Whether the agency, or the producer behind it, holds an Arkansas insurance producer or agency licence.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A state insurance department producer and agency licence lookup for Arkansas, matched to the business and the people on its filing.

body.text: The entity is a Corporation and no people were submitted on the application, so no officer, owner or signer has been verified against the filing and no KYC decision is on the record. The ownership structure is therefore unestablished: who owns and controls the corporation, and who is authorised to sign, rests on an attestation that has not been made.

Two related businesses were found connected to this one. What the connections consist of, and whether any connected business or person sits in the ownership chain, is not established on the record; no related entities were identified beyond those two connections.

gaps.point: Who the beneficial owners, officers and authorised signers of the corporation are, since no people were submitted.
What the two connected businesses are and whether they share ownership or control with this one.

body.text: No UCC or tax liens, no bankruptcy filings and no litigation naming the business were found. For a corporation with an inactive filing and no web footprint, a clean record is consistent with a business that has done little or no trading rather than with an established operating history.
No people were submitted, so lien, litigation and bankruptcy searches on individuals were not run, and no PPP loan search is on the record.

followUps.text:
Request a current Certificate of Good Standing from the Arkansas Secretary of State, or evidence of reinstatement.
The domestic filing is inactive and Arkansas publishes no sub-status, so standing cannot be read from the record.

Collect a beneficial ownership certification naming the owners, officers and authorised signers, and verify them against the filing.
No people were submitted, so nobody behind the corporation has been identified or screened as a signer.

Obtain the IRS CP-575 or 147C letter for the submitted TIN.
The IRS has no record for the submitted TIN and business name combination.

Review the adverse media hit and record its disposition before opening the account.
Adverse media was found on the screening and has not been disposed of.

Obtain the agency's Arkansas insurance producer or agency licence and match it to the business or the people on its filing.
The business is classified as an insurance agency and no licence check is on the record.

Establish what the two connected businesses are and whether they share ownership or control with this one.
Two connections were found and their nature is not on the record.
