olvera`s framing inc.name: Bank account opening
olvera`s framing inc.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to beneficial ownership certification, screening of the owners and signers, and review of the one lien on file.

body.text: OLVERA`S FRAMING INC is a Georgia corporation with one active domestic filing, formed 12 July 2006, and the Georgia registry reports the registration in good standing. The identity check matched the submitted business name to the filing, and the Corporation suffix on the name agrees with the entity type on the record. As typed, the submitted name matches none of the business's filings or DBA names exactly; the filing carries a punctuation variant of the same name, and no DBA was submitted.

The IRS holds a record for the submitted TIN and business name combination. No website was located, so the business name could not be corroborated on the web, and no phone number was submitted. The filing and the TIN together establish a single, distinct, active entity that is the one on the application.

Watchlist screening on the business name returned no hits and no adverse media was found. Politically exposed person screening returned no hits, but no individuals were submitted with the application, so that result covers no owner or signer. No criminal history check has run for the same reason.

gaps.point: Whether the beneficial owners and account signers clear sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening, since no individuals were submitted and the screening to date covers only the business name.

body.text: The business is classified as a framing contractor, which is not a high-risk or prohibited industry under the classification applied. The submitted office address in Georgia matches the state filing, is deliverable by USPS, and is a residential property; the business is active in the state of that address. A residential address is ordinary for a small trade contractor of this age and does not by itself indicate the business operates elsewhere.

No website and no third-party profiles were found, so there is no web evidence of what the business does or where it operates, and the address could not be corroborated online. No contractor licence appears on the record, and whether one is required for framing work at this jurisdiction has not been established.

gaps.point: Whether the business holds a contractor licence for framing work in Georgia, and whether one is required at its scale of work.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A licence lookup for the business or its principal against the Georgia contractor licensing board.

gaps.point: Whether the business is operating as a framing contractor, since no website or profile exists to corroborate the classification.

body.text: No individuals were submitted as owners, officers or signers, so no person has been verified against the record and no KYC decision exists. The entity is a corporation, so beneficial ownership runs through shareholders rather than members. One related business was found connected to this entity; the connection itself does not establish common ownership.

gaps.point: Who owns 25 percent or more of the corporation and who controls it, as no individuals were submitted and none has been verified against the filing.
What the one connected business is and whether it shares ownership with this entity.

body.text: One lien was found against the business; the record does not report the secured party, the collateral or whether the filing is still open. The business has no bankruptcy filings and no related litigation. For a corporation formed in 2006 in the construction trades, a single financing lien is ordinary, but that reading depends on what the filing secures and whether it has lapsed.
No individuals were submitted, so no lien, litigation or bankruptcy search has run on the owners.

gaps.point: What the one lien on file secures, who the secured party is, and whether it remains open.

followUps.text:
Collect a beneficial ownership certification and identification for each 25 percent owner and the controlling officer, and verify them against the Georgia filing.
No individuals were submitted; no person has been verified and no KYC decision exists.

Run sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening on the certified owners and signers.
Screening to date covers only the business name and found no hits.

Pull the lien filing and record the secured party, the collateral and whether it is open or lapsed.
One lien is on file and the record carries no detail on it.

Confirm whether a Georgia contractor licence is required for the business's framing work and, if so, obtain it.
The business is classified as a framing contractor and no licence appears on the record.

Request evidence of operations, such as recent contracts or invoices, and ask the applicant to identify the one connected business.
No website or profile corroborates the line of work, and the connection is on the record without detail.

the coco group llc.name: Bank account opening
the coco group llc.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to IRS confirmation of the TIN, identification and screening of the beneficial owners, evidence of operations at the submitted office address, and a Florida Certificate of Status.

body.text: THE COCO GROUP LLC is a Florida limited liability company with one filing on record, the domestic registration, and it is active. The submitted business name matches that filing and the LLC suffix matches the entity type it carries. Florida publishes no sub-status, so good standing cannot be read from the filing itself and a Certificate of Status is the only source for it.

The IRS holds no record for the submitted TIN and business name together, so the tax identifier on the application is not tied to this entity as filed. The submitted office address is not the address on the Florida filing. No phone number was submitted, no website was located, and no third-party profile was found, so nothing beyond the state filing independently corroborates the name.

gaps.point: Whether the Florida registration is in good standing, since the state does not publish a sub-status on the filing.

body.text: Sanctions and watchlist screening of the business returned no hits, and no adverse media was found against it. Politically exposed person screening returned no hits, but no individuals were submitted on the application, so that result covers nobody in particular; the people side of the screening obligation is open until the owners and signers are named. Criminal history on individuals was not searched for the same reason.

gaps.point: Whether the owners and signers clear sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening, since none were submitted to screen.

body.text: The industry is classified as Employment Placement Agencies and Executive Search Services, and the classification returned no hits against restricted industries. No website URL and no third-party profiles were found, so there is no web evidence of what the business actually does or any second line of activity, and whether it operates as described rests on the application alone.

The submitted office address is a commercial property in Florida, the USPS delivers to it, and the business is active in that state. It does not match the address on the state filing, and with no website there is nothing else on the record placing the business there. No license search ran, so whether the line of work requires a Florida license, and whether one is held, is not covered.

gaps.point: Whether the business operates at the submitted office address, which is not on the filing and is corroborated by nothing on the record.
Whether the business is operating as an employment placement and executive search agency, with no website or profile to corroborate the described activity.
Whether an employment placement agency operating in Florida requires a state license and whether this business holds one.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A license search for the business in Florida, matched to the entity or its officers.

body.text: No owners, officers or signers were submitted with the application, so there is no person on the file to verify against the filing and no KYC decision on anyone. The entity is an LLC, whose members are not on the public filing, so the ownership structure has to come from the applicant's certification rather than the record. Three related businesses were found connected to this entity; the record does not say whether the link is a common officer, a shared address or both, and whether they share ownership is not established.

gaps.point: Who the beneficial owners and authorized signers are, and whether they match the officers on the Florida filing.
What ties this business to the three related businesses found, and whether they share ownership or control.

body.text: No UCC or tax liens, no litigation and no bankruptcy filings were found against the business. For an LLC formed in 2018 in a service trade with no equipment to finance, a clean record is consistent with the line of work rather than notable. No individuals were submitted, so lien, litigation and bankruptcy searches on the owners did not run, and PPP loan data was not pulled; these stand outside the file until the owners are named.

followUps.text:
Obtain the IRS CP-575 or 147C letter for THE COCO GROUP LLC and re-run the TIN match against the name on it.
The IRS holds no record for the submitted TIN and business name together.

Collect the beneficial ownership certification and signer list, verify each person against the Florida filing, and screen them for sanctions, PEP and adverse media.
No individuals were submitted, so nobody on the file has been identified or screened, and the applicant should state how the three connected businesses relate to this one.

Request a lease or utility bill for the submitted office address and a description of services with a recent client contract or invoice.
The office address is not on the state filing and no website or profile corroborates either the address or the stated line of work.

Submit an RFI for a Florida Certificate of Status.
Florida does not publish a sub-status on the filing, so good standing cannot be read from the record.

Confirm whether an employment placement agency in Florida requires a state license and, if so, obtain it.
No license search ran for this business, so the licensing requirement for the industry is not covered.

What does the report show about this address?
Who owns this business?

wilk auslander llp.name: Bank account opening
wilk auslander llp.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to identifying and screening the partners and signers, reviewing the five open liens and ten litigations, and a Certificate of Good Standing from New York.

body.text: WILK AUSLANDER LLP is a registered limited liability partnership with one filing on record, the New York domestic registration, and that filing is active. The submitted business name matches the filing, and the IRS holds a record for the submitted TIN against that name, so the entity on the application is the one registered and the one the IRS recognises. The firm's own website carries the submitted name, which corroborates the registry from an independent source.

New York does not publish a good-standing sub-status for domestic filings, so the record carries the active status alone and no statement on whether the partnership is current with the Department of State. No DBA, phone or foreign registration was submitted, and none was found; the identity file otherwise rests on the registry, the IRS and the website agreeing on a single name.

gaps.point: Whether the New York domestic filing is in good standing, which the state does not publish on the registration.

body.text: The business name returned no sanctions or watchlist hits and no adverse media. The politically exposed persons screen returned no hits on the submitted individuals or their relatives and close associates. On what was screened, nothing triggers a sanctions or enforcement obligation.

The screens ran against the business name and the individuals as submitted; no criminal-history check is on the record. For a partnership, the partners and the authorised signers are the people the obligation attaches to, and until they are named on the file the people-level screening covers only whoever was submitted.

gaps.point: Whether every partner and authorised signer has been screened for sanctions, PEP status and adverse media, since the people screens covered only the individuals submitted.

body.text: The business is classified as Offices of Lawyers, which is not a high-risk or prohibited industry under a standard bank account-opening policy. A website was found and was online when the record was ordered, third-party profiles were found and are all online, and nothing on the web presence points to a line of business other than legal services.

The submitted office address matches the state filing, is a commercial property the USPS can deliver to, and the business is active in the state of that address, so the firm is registered where it operates. The website shows the same office address, which ties the web presence to the registered location.

The practice of law is licensed at the individual level, through each attorney's state bar registration, rather than through a licence held by the firm. No licence check is on the record, so the permission to operate rests on the industry classification and the registry alone.

gaps.point: Whether the partners who will act for the firm hold current New York attorney registrations, as a law practice is licensed through its attorneys rather than the entity.
gaps.wouldAnswer: An attorney-registration lookup against the New York State Unified Court System for each partner and signer.

body.text: The entity is a limited liability partnership, so ownership and control sit with its partners rather than with shareholders or members. No individuals are on the record and no KYC result is held: the registry filing names no officers or partners, and none were verified, so who owns the firm and who is authorised to sign for it is not yet established.

Three related businesses were found through 31 connections. The nature of the connections is not on the record, so whether they are affiliates under common partners, a predecessor firm, or merely businesses sharing a location is open; the ownership structure cannot be called simple or complex until the partners are named.

gaps.point: Who the partners are, what each owns, and who is authorised to sign on the account, since no individuals are on the record and no KYC result is held.
How the firm is connected to the three related businesses and whether any is under common ownership.

body.text: The business has five open liens and is named in ten litigations; it has no bankruptcy filings. The record holds the counts only: the secured parties, what is secured and the filing dates are not on it, nor is the firm's side in each case or whether any money judgment stands against it.

For a law firm, appearing in litigation is ordinary, often as plaintiff collecting fees or as a party to disputes arising from its practice, and an equipment or working-capital lien is ordinary for an established professional office. Five open liens together with ten cases is more than a routine footprint, and the detail decides whether it is ordinary financing and practice litigation or a tax lien or judgment that bears on the account. No individuals were submitted, so no people-level liens, litigation or bankruptcies were searched.

gaps.point: Who the secured parties on the five open liens are, what each secures, and whether any is a tax lien.
Which side the firm is on in each of the ten litigations and whether any carries an outstanding money judgment.

followUps.text:
Obtain the partnership attestation naming each partner, their interest and the authorised signers, verify each identity and screen each for sanctions, PEP status and adverse media.
No individuals are on the record, and the people screens covered only what was submitted.

Review the five open liens for secured party, collateral and whether any is a tax lien.
The record holds the count only, and a tax lien reads differently from equipment finance.

Review the ten litigations for the firm's side in each and any outstanding money judgment.
Litigation is ordinary for a law firm; a judgment against it is not.

Request a Certificate of Good Standing from the New York Department of State.
New York does not publish a sub-status on the domestic filing.

Confirm current New York attorney registration for the partners who will sign on the account.
A law practice is licensed through its attorneys, and no licence check is on the record.

Establish how the firm is connected to the three related businesses and whether any shares its partners.
31 connections are on the record with no account of what links them.

morgan imaging, ltd.name: Bank account opening
morgan imaging, ltd.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to identifying and verifying the partners, since no individual is on the record, and confirming the imaging facility's licensing.

body.text: The submitted name matches the Texas filing for MORGAN IMAGING, LTD, a partnership. One domestic filing is on the record, it is active, and the registry reports it in good standing, so the entity exists as a distinct, current registrant and no good-standing sub-status is outstanding. The IRS holds a record for the submitted TIN and business name together, which ties the tax identity to the registered name.

No foreign filings were found beyond the single domestic registration. No website was located for the business, so the business name could not be corroborated from a web presence; the identity rests on the state filing and the TIN match alone. No DBA names were submitted and no phone was available to verify.

Sanctions and watchlist screening of the business name returned no hits, and no adverse media was found. Politically exposed person screening returned no hits on submitted individuals or their relatives and close associates.
The person-level screenings are only as complete as the people identified to run them against, and no individual sits on this record. Criminal history on the principals was not searched.

gaps.point: Whether the partners and signers clear watchlist, PEP, adverse media and criminal history screening, since no individual is identified on the record.

body.text: The industry is classified as Diagnostic Imaging Centers, which does not fall in a high-risk or prohibited category. The submitted office address matches the filing, the USPS delivers to it, and the property is commercial, which is consistent with an imaging facility. The business is active in the state of that address, so it is registered where it operates.

No website URL and no third-party profiles were found for the business, so the line of work and the office address have no corroboration outside the state filing; the website checks for the address could not be performed. Diagnostic imaging is licensed activity, and no license search was run for this business, so the facility's registrations and their link to an owner or the entity are not on the record.

gaps.point: Whether the facility holds the registrations a diagnostic imaging center requires in Texas and who they are issued to.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A license search for the business name and office address, with person and address match.

gaps.point: Whether imaging services are actually delivered from the office address, as neither a website nor a third-party profile exists to show it.

body.text: The entity is a partnership, so ownership and signing authority sit with its partners, and the partnership agreement is the document that names them. No person was submitted or verified against the record, and no KYC decision exists, so no individual owner or signer is established.

Two related businesses were found, which indicates the business sits within a wider structure, but the record does not say who they are or how they connect. No further related-entity detail is on the record.

gaps.point: Who the partners are, who is authorized to sign, and whether each verifies as an individual.
Whether the two related businesses share ownership or control with this partnership.

body.text: No UCC or tax liens, no litigation and no bankruptcy filings were found against the business. For a recently formed imaging partnership an equipment lien would be ordinary; its absence means nothing on the record encumbers the business or its assets.
Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the partners were not searched, as no person is on the record.

gaps.point: Whether the partners carry liens, litigation or bankruptcies of their own.

followUps.text:
Obtain the partnership agreement, identify each partner and authorized signer, and run person verification with watchlist, PEP, adverse media, criminal history and lien searches on each.
The entity is a partnership and no individual is on the record, so ownership, control and every person-level check are open.

Review the two related businesses for common ownership or control with the partners.
Two connections were found and the record does not say who they are or how they connect.

Confirm the facility holds the registrations a diagnostic imaging center requires in Texas and who they are issued to.
The industry is licensed activity and no license search was run.

Request evidence of operations at the office address, such as a lease or patient-facing materials.
No website or third-party profile exists to corroborate the imaging business beyond the state filing.

quantrex express llc.name: Bank account opening
quantrex express llc.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard QUANTREX EXPRESS LLC subject to clearing the adverse media hit, verifying its owners and confirming its federal operating authority.

body.text: QUANTREX EXPRESS LLC is a real and distinct entity. The submitted name matches a state filing, the LLC suffix agrees with the entity type on that filing, and the single filing on the record is the domestic one, which is active and in good standing. The IRS holds a record for the submitted TIN together with this business name, so the tax identity and the registered identity point at the same entity.

No DBA was submitted and none is at issue. The business has no web presence that names it: no website could be found, so the name could not be corroborated from one. No phone number was returned on the record. For a single-filing LLC in freight trucking, a registered identity resting on the state filing and the TIN match rather than on a website is ordinary and is sufficient for identification.

Sanctions and watchlist screening on the business returned no hits, and politically exposed person screening on the submitted individuals, their relatives and close associates returned no hits. Adverse media was found. The record carries the hit but not what it matched on or whether the subject is this business or a submitted person, so the one screening obligation that is triggered cannot be discharged from the record as it stands.
Criminal history on the submitted people was not returned on this record, so the screening of the individuals rests on the watchlist and PEP results alone.

gaps.point: What the adverse media matched on, and whether the subject is QUANTREX EXPRESS LLC or one of the submitted people rather than a name match to another party.

body.text: The business is classified as General Freight Trucking, Long-Distance, Truckload, which is not a high-risk or prohibited industry under a standard account-opening policy. The submitted office address matches the state filing, the USPS delivers to it, it is a commercial property, and the business is active in the state of that address, so the place it says it operates from is where it is registered. Whether the address is a CMRA or a registered-agent address was not returned, though the commercial classification and the filing match leave little for those checks to add.

No website URL and no third-party profiles were found, and no web source shows the submitted office address, so there is no independent evidence of what the business does beyond the classification. Nothing on the record points to activity in another industry. Interstate for-hire trucking requires federal operating authority, and no licence or operating-authority check is on the record for this business or its people, so permission to operate as classified is not established.

gaps.point: Whether QUANTREX EXPRESS LLC holds active federal operating authority for interstate for-hire freight, and in whose name it is held.
gaps.wouldAnswer: An FMCSA operating authority lookup for the business, returning its USDOT and MC numbers, authority status and the named carrier.

body.text: The entity is an LLC, so ownership sits with its members and is established by the beneficial ownership certification rather than by a public filing. No person was verified against the record: the submitted people were not matched to the registration or to any other source, and no KYC decision is on the record for them. Who owns and controls the business, and whether the submitted signers are those people, is therefore unestablished.

Three related businesses were found. The record does not say what links them to QUANTREX EXPRESS LLC or who stands behind them, and no related entities were returned by name. For a single-member or family trucking LLC a handful of connected businesses is unremarkable, but the ownership structure cannot be called simple until the three are read against the submitted owners.

gaps.point: Whether the submitted owners and signers are the people behind QUANTREX EXPRESS LLC, since none was matched to the record and no KYC decision is held.
What connects the three related businesses to QUANTREX EXPRESS LLC, and whether they share an owner with it.

body.text: The business carries no UCC or tax liens, no litigation and no bankruptcy filings. For a trucking company formed in 2021 an equipment lien would have been ordinary, so a clean lien search says little either way; the absence of tax liens, litigation and insolvency is what bears on the account, and all three searches were run and returned nothing.

Liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people were not returned on this record, and no PPP loan result is held. The financial standing of the business is established; that of the people behind it is not.

gaps.point: Whether the submitted owners carry liens, litigation or bankruptcy filings in their own names.

followUps.text:
Review the adverse media hit and record whether its subject is QUANTREX EXPRESS LLC or a submitted person, or a name match to another party.
Adverse media was found and the record does not say what it matched on; it is the only screening that returned a hit.

Collect the beneficial ownership certification and run KYC on each named owner and signer.
No submitted person was matched to the record and no KYC decision is held, so ownership and signing authority of the LLC are unestablished.

Look up the business on the FMCSA register and record its USDOT and MC numbers, authority status and the named carrier.
The business is classified as long-distance truckload freight, which requires federal operating authority, and no licence check is on the record.

Read the three related businesses on the record against the certified owners and note any shared owner.
The record reports three connections but not what links them to the business or who is behind them.

Order lien, litigation and bankruptcy searches on the certified owners.
The business itself is clear, but the people searches were not returned on this record.

douglas g brown.name: Bank account opening
douglas g brown.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

body.text: DOUGLAS G BROWN is a sole proprietorship operating under the proprietor's own name. The submitted business name was matched, and the IRS holds a record for the submitted TIN and business name combination, so the name, the taxpayer and the entity type line up on the record.

The business has no Secretary of State filings, and the submitted name matches no state filing or DBA on file. A sole proprietorship trading under the proprietor's legal name files nothing with a Secretary of State, so there is no domestic registration, no formation state and no good-standing sub-status to verify. Third-party web sources show a name similar to the submitted name; no business phone or email was submitted.

gaps.point: Whether a domestic registration is active and in good standing.
gaps.noAction: A sole proprietorship trading under the proprietor's own name holds no Secretary of State registration, so there is no standing to certify.

body.text: Sanctions and watchlist screening of the business returned no hits, adverse media screening returned no results, and PEP screening of the submitted individuals and their relatives and close associates returned no hits. No criminal-history search was run on the submitted people.

Industry classification returned insufficient data, so the line of work is not established on the record and no eligibility, licensing or jurisdiction check can be read against it. No license record is on file.

The submitted office address was matched, is USPS-deliverable and is a residential property, which is ordinary for a sole proprietorship run from the proprietor's home. The business holds no registration in the state of that address, consistent with its having no state filings at all. No website URL was found; third-party profiles were found and are online, and none of them shows the submitted office address.

gaps.point: What the business does, and whether that activity is eligible under policy.
Whether the activity requires a license in the state of operation, and whether the proprietor holds one.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A license search against the proprietor's name and state once the line of work is known.

body.text: As a sole proprietorship the business has one owner and one signer by form, Douglas G Brown, with no entity owners, officers or registered agents to identify and no ownership structure beyond the individual. No related businesses were found.
No person verification result and no KYC decision are on the record, so the proprietor's identity has not been verified against the business.

gaps.point: Whether the individual on the application is Douglas G Brown and is the person behind the business.

body.text: No UCC or tax liens and no bankruptcy filings were found against the business. Nine related litigations were found; the record does not show which side the business is on, the status of each case or whether any carries a money judgment.
For a sole proprietorship the proprietor's own debts are the business's, and no lien, litigation or bankruptcy search was run against the proprietor as an individual.

gaps.point: The role of the business in each of the nine litigations, the status of each case and any money judgment.
Whether Douglas G Brown as an individual carries liens, litigation or a bankruptcy.

followUps.text:
Pull the nine litigation records and establish the business's role, each case's status and any money judgment.
The record counts nine related litigations but shows nothing of what they are.

Verify Douglas G Brown's identity and run KYC on him as owner and signer.
A sole proprietorship has one owner by form, and no person verification or KYC decision is on the record.

Obtain a description of the business activity from the applicant and run the license check that activity requires.
Industry classification returned insufficient data, so eligibility and licensing cannot be read from the record.

Order lien, litigation and bankruptcy searches on Douglas G Brown as an individual.
The proprietor's debts are the business's, and none of those searches was run on him.

district 1 property solutions llc.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated

body.text: DISTRICT 1 PROPERTY SOLUTIONS LLC matches the submitted name on one active domestic Connecticut filing, the only filing on the record; the entity is an LLC and the name suffix agrees with the filing. The IRS holds a record for the submitted TIN and business name combination, so the tax identity ties to the same legal entity.

The website presents a name similar to, rather than identical with, the legal name, and no DBA filing is on the record. No phone was returned on the record, and none was submitted, so it is not verified here.

gaps.point: Whether the LLC is in good standing: Connecticut publishes an active status but no good-standing sub-status.

body.text: The watchlist screen on the business returned no hits, and the PEP screen returned no hits on submitted individuals or their relatives and close associates. No people are on the record, so the person-level sanctions and PEP screens have nothing to run against beyond the name search already done.
The adverse media screen returned a finding. The record carries no detail of the item or of who it is matched to, so it cannot be dispositioned from the report alone.

gaps.point: What the adverse media item concerns and whether it is matched to this business rather than a namesake.
Criminal history on the people behind the business.
gaps.noAction: No people are on the record to screen and the check is not a standard requirement for a deposit account; the watchlist and PEP screens are clear.

body.text: The business classifies as Janitorial Services, outside high-risk and prohibited categories, and nothing on the record points to another line of work. Janitorial work in Connecticut carries no state occupational licence, so no licence check applies.

The submitted office address matches the state filing, is a deliverable commercial property and appears on the business's website; the business is active in the state of that address. A website was found and was online when the record was ordered. No third-party profiles were found, which is ordinary for a small services business formed in 2022.

gaps.point: Whether the business holds a licence for its line of work.
gaps.noAction: Janitorial services are not a licensed occupation in Connecticut; no licence is required of the industry in this jurisdiction.

body.text: No people are on the record: none were submitted and the Connecticut LLC filing publishes no members or managers on this record, so neither the owners nor an authorised signer is established. No identity verification has been run. For an LLC the beneficial ownership certification has to name each owner at or above the threshold and the control person, and nothing on the record yet does.

Four related businesses were found. The record does not say what links them, whether a shared address, a shared person or a shared agent, so the ownership structure cannot be read as simple or layered from the report alone.

body.text: The business has no UCC or tax liens, no bankruptcy filings and no related litigation on record, consistent with a janitorial services LLC formed in 2022 with no financed equipment or disputes to date. Nothing at the business level bears on the account.

wright way customs.name: Bank account opening
wright way customs.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated

report.headline: Onboard subject to identifying and verifying the proprietor, screening and searching them personally, and obtaining evidence of the trade name and of operations at the address.

body.text: WRIGHT WAY CUSTOMS was submitted as a sole proprietorship, and the record carries no Secretary of State filing for it in any state. The submitted name matched no state registration or DBA on file, and no formation state, filing status or sub-status is available, since no filing exists to carry them. For a sole proprietorship this is the expected shape: the business is the individual, and nothing is registered with a Secretary of State unless the owner files an assumed name.

The IRS holds a record for the submitted TIN against the business name, which ties the name to a taxpayer. No website or third-party profile was found, so the business name could not be corroborated from a web presence, and no phone was returned on the record.

gaps.point: Whether WRIGHT WAY CUSTOMS is a registered assumed name of a named individual is not established, as no state or DBA filing was found and county-level assumed-name registers are not searched.

body.text: Watchlist screening of the business returned no hits, and no adverse media was found. Politically exposed person screening returned no hits on submitted individuals or their relatives and close associates.
No individual is on the record for this business, so the screening results rest on the business name alone. Criminal history for people returned nothing on this record.

gaps.point: The proprietor has not been screened for sanctions, PEP status, adverse media or criminal history, because no individual is on the record.

body.text: The industry is classified as All Other Miscellaneous Textile Product Mills, which is not a high-risk or prohibited industry and carries no industry licence requirement at the state level. No licence is on the record and none would be expected for this classification.

The submitted office address is a commercial property to which the USPS delivers mail. It could not be matched to a filing, and the business is not registered in the state of that address, which follows from there being no Secretary of State filing at all. Whether the address is a CMRA or a registered-agent address was not returned.

No website URL and no third-party profiles were found for the business, so there is no web evidence of the address or of the line of work, and whether the business operates as claimed is not established on the record.

gaps.point: Nothing on the record shows the business trading in textile products from the submitted address, as there is no website, no profile and no filing naming the address.

body.text: The business is a sole proprietorship, so the owner, the controller and the signer are the same individual and there is no ownership structure beyond that person. No individual was submitted or found on the record, no KYC result is held, and no related businesses were found.

gaps.point: The individual who owns and signs for WRIGHT WAY CUSTOMS is not identified on the record, so the beneficial-ownership attestation cannot be checked against anything.

body.text: No liens, litigation or bankruptcy filings were found against the business. No PPP loan is on the record.

For a sole proprietorship the owner's personal debts and judgments are the business's, and the people-level lien, litigation and bankruptcy searches returned nothing on this record because no individual is on it.

gaps.point: Liens, litigation and bankruptcies against the proprietor personally have not been searched, and for a sole proprietorship those are the business's obligations.

The business is a sole proprietorship with no individual on the record, so the owner and signer are unverified.

Screen the proprietor for sanctions, PEP status, adverse media and criminal history once identified.
The screening on file ran against the business name only.

Run lien, litigation and bankruptcy searches against the proprietor personally.
A sole proprietor's personal obligations are the business's, and only the business-level searches have run.

Request the assumed-name certificate for WRIGHT WAY CUSTOMS, or the proprietor's confirmation that none is held.
No state filing or DBA on file carries the name, and it is not a personal name.

Request evidence of operations at the submitted address, such as a lease or recent invoices.
No website, profile or filing places the business there.

sara stubbs.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank.

✨ Sometimes, we need someone to believe in us before we can believe in ourselves. ✨

There are days when self-doubt gets loud.

“I can’t do this.”
“What if I get it wrong?”
“Everyone else seems to manage this better than me.”
“Maybe I’m just not good at it.”

But struggling doesn’t mean you’re failing.
Needing support doesn’t mean you’re incapable.
Taking longer doesn’t mean you’re behind.

Sometimes, you just need someone beside you who can see your strengths when you’re struggling to see them yourself. 💛

At Equity Educators, we believe in walking alongside you — not doing things for you, but supporting you to discover what works for you.

We’ll celebrate the wins, sit with the hard days, help you find your next step, and remind you of what you’re capable of when self-doubt takes over.

You don’t have to believe in yourself every single day.

On the days you can’t,
we’ve got your back. 💛

#EquityEducators #SelfBelief #NeuroAffirming #YouveGotThis #DisabilitySupport NDIS StrengthsBased YouAreCapable NeurodivergentSupport DevelopmentalEducator

18 days, 3 countries, countless memories ❤️
From the magic of Paris, to the beauty of Florence, the coastal charm of Cinque Terre, and the history of Rome… what a journey it’s been.

We’ve walked everywhere, explored, eaten (a lot 😄), and filled our days with moments we’ll never forget ….including a pasta making class for my 60th and a sunrise bike ride through Rome.

So many photos, but even more memories.
Ending tomorrow with very full hearts (and very full camera rolls). 🇫🇷🇮🇹✨

Wow 🤩 
What an incredible day ❤️ celebrating Maddy and Phil’s love.

🌟 To our neurodivergent community 

If today feels heavy or hard 
If you’re questioning your worth or wondering if you’re “enough” 
Please borrow this belief:

✨ we believe in you.
We believe in the way your brain works, even when others don’t understand it.
We believe in your unique rhythm, your brilliance, your way.
We believe that you are not too much and NEVER not enough.

So if your own belief feels far away today
Here, take mine.
Hold onto it until yours returns.
Because it will. 💛

#NeurodivergentAndProud #YouAreEnough #NeurodivergentVoices #BorrowMyBelief #MentalHealthMatters #AutismAcceptance #ADHDAwareness #PDAAwareness #NeurodiversityAffirming #WeSeeYou

Connection first, always. 🌟

When it comes to supporting any child — and especially our neurodivergent students — connection is the key to co-regulation. 💛

It’s through trust, safety, and authentic relationships that we help children feel seen, heard, and safe enough to regulate alongside us. Before we teach, correct, or redirect… we connect. 🤝

✨ Remember: regulation isn’t taught through control — it’s shared through calm, compassion, and connection.

#NeurodivergentAffirming #CoRegulation #ConnectionBeforeCorrection #Neurodiversity #InclusiveEducation #SafeRelationships #ConnectedKids #NeurodivergentSupport #CompassionateClassroom

**The First Few Weeks: Easing Into the School Year** 

The start of a new school year can bring excitement, but for our neurodivergent children, it can also bring exhaustion, overwhelm, and big emotions. The first few weeks aren’t about academic success or meeting milestones—they’re about *safety, connection, and relationships.* 

✨ **Decrease expectations** – Learning will happen when they feel secure. For now, focus on helping them settle in. 

✨ **Release comparison** – Every child’s journey is unique. Trust that your child is growing in their own way, at their own pace. 

✨ **Prioritise regulation** – If they’re coming home tired, dysregulated, or melting down, it doesn’t mean they’re failing. It means they’re using all their energy just to get through the day. 

Give them time, space, and understanding. Their well-being comes first—everything else will follow. 

#NeurodivergentKids #BackToSchool #SafetyConnectionRegulation #TrustTheProcess#neurowild

**✨ On the Eve of 2025 ✨** 

As the clock ticks down on 2024, I find myself reflecting on a year filled with growth, challenges, and unforgettable moments. 🌟 

This year has brought highs that lit up my heart and lows that tested my resilience. Each step—whether steady or shaky—has shaped me and reminded me of the power of perseverance, connection, and hope. 💫 

To those who have shared this journey with me, thank you for your kindness, laughter, and unwavering support. Here’s to embracing the lessons of 2024 and welcoming 2025 with open hearts and boundless possibilities. 

Wishing you all a year ahead filled with love, growth, and joy. 🕊️ 
**Let’s make it count!** 

#NewYearReflections #Goodbye2024 #Hello2025 #Gratitude #GrowthJourney

🎄✨ **Release the pressure this Christmas!** ✨🎄 

Your little ones won’t stay little forever. Before you know it, they’ll be grown and off creating their own traditions. 

Let them eat the chocolate, stay up late, and soak in every second of the magic. 🎁🌟 

This season is about joy, wonder, and connection—see Christmas through their eyes and cherish these fleeting moments. 

Here’s to a holiday filled with love, laughter, and the little things that matter most. ❤️ 

#ChristmasMagic #FamilyTime #CherishTheMoment #LetKidsBeKids

✨ **Decrease expectations** – Learning will happen when they feel secure. For now, focus on helping them settle in. 

✨ **Release comparison** – Every child’s journey is unique. Trust that your child is growing in their own way, at their own pace. 

✨ **Prioritise regulation** – If they’re coming home tired, dysregulated, or melting down, it doesn’t mean they’re failing. It means they’re using all their energy just to get through the day. 

Give them time, space, and understanding. Their well-being comes first—everything else will follow. 

#NeurodivergentKids #BackToSchool #SafetyConnectionRegulation #TrustTheProcess#neurowild

**✨ On the Eve of 2025 ✨** 

As the clock ticks down on 2024, I find myself reflecting on a year filled with growth, challenges, and unforgettable moments. 🌟 

This year has brought highs that lit up my heart and lows that tested my resilience. Each step—whether steady or shaky—has shaped me and reminded me of the power of perseverance, connection, and hope. 💫 

To those who have shared this journey with me, thank you for your kindness, laughter, and unwavering support. Here’s to embracing the lessons of 2024 and welcoming 2025 with open hearts and boundless possibilities. 

Wishing you all a year ahead filled with love, growth, and joy. 🕊️ 
**Let’s make it count!** 

#NewYearReflections #Goodbye2024 #Hello2025 #Gratitude #GrowthJourney

🎄✨ **Release the pressure this Christmas!** ✨🎄 

Your little ones won’t stay little forever. Before you know it, they’ll be grown and off creating their own traditions. 

Let them eat the chocolate, stay up late, and soak in every second of the magic. 🎁🌟 

This season is about joy, wonder, and connection—see Christmas through their eyes and cherish these fleeting moments. 

Here’s to a holiday filled with love, laughter, and the little things that matter most. ❤️ 

#ChristmasMagic #FamilyTime #CherishTheMoment #LetKidsBeKids

🌈💔 Yesterday, our beloved 11-year-old Labrador, Archie, peacefully drifted off to sleep for the last time. He was there for us through some of life’s hardest moments, always by our side with that wagging tail and gentle eyes. Archie was more than a pet; he was family, a friend, and such a special soul who filled our days with love. Our hearts are broken, but we’ll cherish his memory forever. Run free, sweet boy. 🐾💫
