amiora ai, inc..name: Bank account opening
amiora ai, inc..brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

body.text: AMIORA AI, INC. is a Delaware corporation. The submitted name matches a state filing, the "INC." suffix agrees with the corporation entity type on that filing, and the IRS holds a record for the submitted TIN against this business name, so the applicant is the registered entity and the tax identity ties to it.

Delaware publishes neither a filing status nor a sub-status, so whether the corporation is active and in good standing cannot be read from the registry; it is a limit of the source, not a finding against the business. No website was located, so there is no web statement of the business name to compare, and no phone number was submitted for verification.

gaps.point: Whether the Delaware corporation is active and in good standing, which the state does not publish.

body.text: Screening of the business name returned no sanctions or watchlist hits and no adverse media. The submitted individuals, together with their relatives and close associates, returned no politically exposed person hits. Nothing on the record triggers a sanctions, PEP or enforcement obligation.
A criminal history search on the submitted people was not run on this record, so that check is absent rather than clear.

The business is classified as Custom Computer Programming Services, an industry that is neither high-risk nor prohibited and that carries no licensing requirement, so no license search applies. No website URL and no third-party profiles were found, which means the line of work rests on the classification alone; there is no independent evidence that the business operates as claimed.

The submitted office address matches the state filing, is deliverable and is a commercial property, but it is the address of a known registered agent. For a Delaware corporation that is the ordinary arrangement for the filing; it is not a place of operations, and with no website to show an address the record does not establish where the business actually works from.

gaps.point: Where the business actually operates, since the only address on the record is a registered agent's and no web presence names another.
gaps.wouldAnswer: An operating address from the applicant, corroborated by a lease, utility bill or similar document.

gaps.point: Whether the business operates as a software developer, which nothing beyond the industry classification currently corroborates.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A product URL, customer contract or description of services from the applicant that can be checked against the classification.

body.text: No person verification result is on the record, so no officer, director or owner of the corporation has been matched to a filing and the beneficial ownership structure is not established. No KYC decision has been recorded for any individual.

No related businesses were found, and no related entities were identified, so there is no indication of a parent, affiliate or shared-ownership structure behind the corporation. As a corporation, ownership is by shareholding and control sits with the directors and officers, each of whom the attestation would need to name.

gaps.point: Who owns 25 percent or more of the corporation and who controls it, since no person on the record has been verified or passed KYC.

body.text: The business has no UCC or tax liens, no bankruptcy filings and no litigation naming it. A clean record is consistent with a newly formed software corporation that has had little occasion to borrow against assets or be sued, and nothing here bears on the account.

Lien, litigation and bankruptcy searches on the submitted people were not run, and no PPP loan result is on the record, so the individuals behind the business have not been checked for personal debts or insolvency.

gaps.point: Whether the owners and signers carry liens, judgments or bankruptcies, which has not been searched.

The only address on file is a registered agent's and no website or profiles were found, so where and how the business operates is not on the record.

Run lien, litigation and bankruptcy searches on the owners and signers once they are named.
The business record is clean but the people searches were not run.

parafin, inc..name: Bank account opening
parafin, inc..brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:

body.text: PARAFIN, INC. is a corporation. The submitted business name matches a state filing, its suffix matches the entity type on the filing, and the IRS holds a record for the submitted TIN and business name combination. The website shows the submitted business name.

The domestic filing is in Delaware, which publishes neither a filing status nor a sub-status, so good standing cannot be read from the registry. Fourteen Secretary of State filings are on the record: twelve are active and one is inactive. No DBA, phone or email was submitted, so none was verified.

body.text: The industry is classified as Consumer Lending, within Investment and Credit Services. Lending is a licensed activity in most states, and no licence check is on the record, so whether the business holds the lending licences its line of work requires where it operates is not established.

The submitted office address matches the record, is a commercial property, and the USPS can deliver to it. The business is active in the state of that address. body.text: The entity is a corporation. No person is on the record: no officer, owner or signer was submitted or verified, and no KYC decision is held, so who owns and controls the corporation and who is authorised to sign is not established.

Parafin offers loans with a one time capital fee, instead of a loan with interest, to confused business owners. The loan they offered me was equivalent to a 65% APR. I appreciated the offer, but giving out loans of this rate should not be legal, as I'm sure many small businesses don't know any better. They also collect the loan based on your sales numbers, meaning the more sales you make, the faster you have to pay it off.

Extremely frustrating experience with Parafin. I am only giving one star for the nice woman who actually took time to help me on my first call that happened to be a strike of luck.

On Friday, March 13, I was able to speak with a representative so I know it’s possible to get real support. However, since then, my experience has been the complete opposite.

We are currently dealing with an urgent payroll situation tied to their Payroll Bridge product through Gusto for two separate companies, and getting real-time assistance has been nearly impossible. I have called multiple times, left voicemails, and requested callbacks repeatedly over the past several days—yet no one has returned a single call. Instead, they continue to respond only via email, despite me clearly explaining how time-sensitive this situation is. It was to the point they started forwarding all of my calls to voicemail.

What makes this even more frustrating is the constant runaround. Parafin keeps pointing the issue back to Gusto, saying it’s a technical problem. When I contacted Gusto, they informed me that a third-party (Melio) placed a block on the account. I have relayed this information back to Parafin multiple times, but they continue redirecting me to Gusto without actually investigating or taking ownership. I’m essentially stuck in the middle with no clear answers.

At this point, if Parafin does not return my call and help resolve this issue as soon as possible Causing me to have to take the Financial blow during the one time I actually needed this type of assistance, I would not recommend them—especially for something as critical as payroll-related funding across multiple companies. When employees need to be paid, responsive and accountable support isn’t optional, it’s essential!

Very disappointing experience.

Serious Issues with Unauthorized Charges & Incorrect Data Handling I am extremely disappointed with my experience with Parafin. They have mishandled my account, made unauthorized fund withdrawals, and relied on incorrect data, causing severe disruptions to my business operations. Unauthorized Charges: My repayment schedule was supposed to be bi-weekly, yet they deducted payments weekly without my consent. Despite multiple requests, they have failed to refund the excess charges. Incorrect Data & Unjustified Charges: They sent me an email claiming incorrect data from Amazon led to additional charges. This is unacceptable, as I am not responsible for their data errors. Even after raising objections, they continued withdrawing funds arbitrarily. Business Disruptions: These unauthorized deductions and unjustified charges have left my account in deficit, preventing me from purchasing inventory for my Amazon business. This has severely impacted my cash flow and business stability. I demand immediate resolution, including a full refund of unauthorized overcharges, a stop to further unauthorized deductions, and transparency regarding the data discrepancy. If they do not act promptly, I will escalate the matter legally and through consumer protection authorities. I am also in contact with other affected individuals who are considering collective action. I strongly advise caution to anyone considering using Parafin’s services. Their unethical practices have caused significant financial harm. I expect an urgent response within 7 days, failing which I will take further action, including publicly exposing their unfair practices.

After a rocky start last year I was skeptical of accepting a new cash advance. However I spoke with an extremely competent woman at Parafin who addressed all my concerns and assured me their system had been updated and I could move ahead with confidence. The future of small business financing may look a lot more like software.

Platforms already sit at the center of how millions of small businesses run. They see how those businesses are performing and often know when they’re preparing to invest, hire, or manage a cash flow gap.

That puts platforms in a powerful position to deliver financing at the moment it’s useful, directly inside the tools their customers already rely on.

noe pierre louis llc.name: Bank account opening
noe pierre louis llc.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to a beneficial ownership certification and KYC on the members, confirmation of the Florida real estate licence, and a Florida Certificate of Status.

body.text: NOE PIERRE LOUIS LLC is a Florida limited liability company with one filing on record, the domestic registration, and that filing is active. The submitted business name matches the filing and its LLC suffix agrees with the entity type the filing carries, so the name on the application is the registered one. The IRS holds a record for the submitted TIN against this business name, which ties the tax identity to the same entity.

Florida does not publish a good-standing sub-status on the domestic filing, so the record shows the registration as active and nothing further about its standing. No foreign registrations are on file. No website was found for the business, so the web check could not confirm the business name from a site, and no phone number was submitted for verification.

gaps.point: Whether the Florida registration is in good standing is not published on the filing.

body.text: Sanctions and watchlist screening of the business returned no hits, and adverse media screening returned no results. Politically exposed person screening on the submitted individuals, their relatives and close associates also returned no hits. Nothing on the record triggers a sanctions or enforcement obligation.

A criminal history check on the people behind the business did not run on this record. Once the members are identified for the ownership certification, the screenings above should be read against those named individuals rather than the business alone.

The business is classified as Offices of Real Estate Agents and Brokers, which is not a high-risk or prohibited industry under a standard bank policy. Real estate brokerage is licensed activity in Florida, and no licence check ran on this record, so whether the entity or a qualifying broker behind it holds an active licence is not established. No website or third-party profile was found, so there is no independent evidence of what the business does beyond the classification, and the operating-as-claimed check did not run.

The submitted office address is a residential property to which the USPS delivers, and the record identified an address within 0.2 miles of it rather than an exact match. The business is active in Florida, the state of that address, so no foreign registration question arises. A residential address is ordinary for a single-agent real estate LLC. Whether the address is a commercial mail receiving agency or a registered agent's was not checked, and with no website the web check could not match the address to a site.

gaps.point: Whether the business or its qualifying broker holds an active Florida real estate licence is not on the record.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A licence check against the Florida DBPR real estate licensee roll for the entity and its principal.

gaps.point: Nothing beyond the industry classification evidences that the business operates as a real estate brokerage.

body.text: No person was verified against the business on this record and no KYC decision was returned, so the member or members of the LLC, and who is authorised to sign, are not established. The entity is an LLC, so the structure is expected to be simple, but no owner, officer or registered agent is on the record to confirm that.
Two related businesses were found. The record does not say what links them to this entity or whether a common owner is behind them, and no related-entity check ran.

gaps.point: Who owns and controls the LLC is not on the record, and no KYC has been run on anyone behind it.
What links the two related businesses to this entity, and whether they share an owner, is not on the record.

body.text: The business carries no UCC or tax liens, is named in no litigation and has no bankruptcy filings. For a real estate brokerage LLC a clean record is the expected position, and nothing here bears on the account.
No people were submitted, so lien, litigation and bankruptcy searches on the individuals behind the business did not run, and no PPP loan check ran on this record.

followUps.text:
Obtain the beneficial ownership certification naming the members and signer of NOE PIERRE LOUIS LLC and run KYC on each.
No person was verified against the business and no KYC decision is on the record.

Confirm an active Florida real estate licence for the entity or its qualifying broker against the DBPR licensee roll.
The business is classified as a real estate brokerage, which is licensed activity, and no licence check ran.

Submit an RFI for a Florida Certificate of Status.
The filing is active but Florida does not publish a good-standing sub-status.

Identify the two related businesses and whether they share an owner with this entity.
Two connections were found and the record does not say what links them.

Request one document evidencing current brokerage activity, such as a listing agreement or commission statement.
No website or profile was found and the operating-as-claimed check did not run, so only the classification speaks to what the business does.

jc swimming pool & spa service.name: Bank account opening
jc swimming pool & spa service.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to identifying and verifying the proprietor, confirming the TIN against the owner's name, and reviewing the three litigations.

body.text: JC SWIMMING POOL & SPA SERVICE is a sole proprietorship. The record holds no Secretary of State filing for it, domestic or foreign, and no filing status or sub-status, which is the expected position for an unincorporated trade operated under the owner's own name: there is no registration for a good-standing certificate to attach to.

The submitted name returned a similar match rather than an exact one, and it matches no state filing or assumed-name filing on file. The business name does appear on the web, so the trade name is in use, but nothing on the record ties that name to a registered filing or to a named proprietor.

The IRS holds no record for the submitted TIN and business name together. For a sole proprietorship the TIN is ordinarily the owner's SSN or an EIN issued in the owner's name, so a non-match against the trade name does not by itself show the number is wrong; it leaves the TIN unverified until it is checked against the name it was issued to. No phone result is on the record.

gaps.point: Whether the submitted TIN was issued to the proprietor, since the IRS has no record of it against the trade name.
Whether a fictitious or assumed-name filing exists for the trade name in the county or state where the business operates.

body.text: Watchlist screening of the business name returned no hits and no adverse media was found. The politically exposed person screen returned no hits on submitted individuals or their relatives and close associates; no criminal history result is on the record. The business-level screens are therefore clear, and no sanctions or enforcement obligation is triggered on what was screened.

The people screens can only cover the individuals submitted, and the record does not establish who the proprietor is. Until the owner is named and screened, the sanctions, PEP and adverse media results stand for the business name alone.

gaps.point: Whether the proprietor clears sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening once identified.

body.text: The industry is classified as Other Services to Buildings and Dwellings, consistent with the pool and spa servicing the name describes, and it is not flagged as a high-risk or prohibited industry. No license check ran on this record, so whether pool service contracting is licensed in the operating jurisdiction, and whether the proprietor holds that license, is not something the record answers.

The submitted office address matched the record and the USPS can deliver to it. It is a residential property, and the business is not registered in that state. Both are ordinary for a sole proprietorship run from the owner's home, and neither counts against the business on its own.

No website URL was found, so the web checks have no site to read: the office address was not seen online. Third-party profiles were found and all are online, which is the only independent evidence on the record that the business is operating. Nothing on the record confirms it operates as claimed beyond those profiles.

gaps.point: Whether a pool or spa service contractor license is required where the business operates and, if so, whether the proprietor holds one.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A license search for the business and the proprietor in the state and county of the office address.

body.text: As a sole proprietorship the business has one owner, who is also its only authorized signer, so the ownership structure is as simple as it can be. No person result is on the record, however, and no KYC decision has been reached: the proprietor has not been identified or verified, which leaves the control question open despite the simple structure.
No related businesses were found and no related-entity result is on the record, so there is no sign of a wider structure or of other entities sharing the owner or the address.

gaps.point: Who the proprietor is, and whether that individual passes identity verification as the sole owner and signer.

body.text: No UCC or tax liens and no bankruptcy filings were found against the business. Three related litigations were found. The record does not say which side the business is on, whether any carries a money judgment, or when they were filed, and for a service trade of this kind three suits against a sole proprietor would bear on the account differently from three collection actions it brought.

No people-level lien, litigation or bankruptcy results are on the record, and no PPP loan result. For a sole proprietorship the owner's personal debts are the business's debts, so the business-level clear results cover only half the picture until the proprietor is named and searched.

gaps.point: What the three related litigations are, which party the business is, and whether any resulted in a judgment.
Whether the proprietor personally carries liens, litigation or bankruptcy filings.

followUps.text:
Obtain the proprietor's name and government ID and run person verification and screening.
The record identifies no individual behind the business, so the owner and sole signer is unverified and unscreened.

Pull the three related litigation records and note the business's role and any judgment.
The record shows three suits but not which side the business is on or what they resolved to.

Re-verify the TIN against the proprietor's name once it is known.
The IRS has no record of the TIN against the trade name, which is expected for a sole proprietorship whose number was issued to the owner.

Run lien, litigation and bankruptcy searches on the proprietor.
The business-level results are clear, but a sole proprietor's personal debts are the business's debts.

Request a copy of the assumed-name filing for the trade name, or confirm none is required in the operating jurisdiction.
The submitted name matched no state filing or DBA on file.

Confirm whether a contractor license is required for pool and spa service where the business operates and obtain it if so.
No license check ran on this record.

What do the three litigations involve?
Who owns this business?

stllr network inc..name: Bank account opening
stllr network inc..brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to a beneficial ownership certification with screening of the named owners, a Delaware Certificate of Good Standing, and evidence of the operating address.

body.text: STLLR NETWORK INC. is a Delaware corporation. The submitted business name matches the state filing, the name's suffix agrees with the entity type on that filing, and the IRS holds a record for the submitted TIN and business name together. The website carries a name similar to, rather than identical with, the submitted name; third-party profiles for the business are found and online, so the entity is a distinct and discoverable one.

Delaware publishes neither a filing status nor a sub-status for its domestic entities, so the record cannot show whether the corporation is active and in good standing. This is a limit of the registry rather than a finding against the business; standing has to be evidenced by a certificate obtained from the state. No DBA, phone or email was submitted, so none was verified.

gaps.point: Whether the Delaware corporation is active and in good standing, since the state publishes no status or sub-status for the domestic filing.

body.text: Screening of the business name returned no watchlist or sanctions hits and no adverse media. The politically exposed persons search returned no hits on submitted individuals or their relatives and close associates. No sanctions or enforcement obligation is triggered by anything on the record.

No individuals were submitted with the application, so no owner or signer has been screened by name and the criminal-history search did not run. Person-level sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening is outstanding until the beneficial owners and signers are identified.

gaps.point: Whether the beneficial owners and signers clear sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening, since no individuals were submitted to screen.

body.text: The business is classified as an advertising agency, which is neither a high-risk nor a prohibited industry and does not require a trade licence in any jurisdiction, so no licence is expected on the record and none is found. Third-party profiles for the business are found and all are online. Nothing on the record points to activity in another line of business.

The submitted office address matches the state filing, is a deliverable commercial property, and is associated with a known registered agent; the state of that address does not publish filing status. A registered-agent address is ordinary for a Delaware corporation but is not where the business operates. No website URL was found by discovery, yet the web check that did run shows an address different from the submitted office, so the operating location is not established by the record.

gaps.point: Where the business actually operates, since the submitted office is a registered-agent address and the web check shows a different address.
Which website belongs to the business, since URL discovery returned nothing while the web checks report content under a similar name.
Whether an operating licence is required for the line of work.
gaps.noAction: Advertising agencies are not a licensed trade; no licence is required in any jurisdiction.

body.text: No individuals were submitted as owners, officers or signers, so no person has been matched to the corporation and no KYC decision exists on the record. The entity is a corporation, and a Delaware corporation discloses no officers or shareholders on its public filing, so the record itself carries no ownership information to compare an attestation against.

No related businesses were found, and no related-entities result is held, so there is no indication on the record of a layered or multi-entity ownership structure. The beneficial ownership certification and identification of the control person remain outstanding.

gaps.point: Who the beneficial owners and control person are, since no individuals were submitted and the Delaware filing names none.

body.text: Searches for UCC and tax liens, litigation and bankruptcy filings against the business all returned nothing: no liens are recorded, no litigation names the business, and the business has no bankruptcy filings. For an advertising agency formed in Delaware, a clean record of this kind is consistent with a young service business that has not taken on secured debt.
No individuals were submitted, so no person-level lien, litigation or bankruptcy search ran, and no PPP loan result is held on the record.

followUps.text:
Obtain the beneficial ownership certification, identify the control person and run KYC on each named individual.
No individuals were submitted and the Delaware filing names none, so ownership and control rest on nothing yet.

Screen each named owner and signer for sanctions, PEP and adverse media once the certification is in.
Only the business name has been screened; no person has been.

Submit an RFI for a Delaware Certificate of Good Standing.
Delaware publishes no filing status or sub-status, so standing cannot be read from the record.

Obtain evidence of the operating address, such as a lease or utility bill.
The submitted office is a registered-agent address and the web check shows a different one.

Ask the applicant for the business website URL and confirm the name and address shown on it.
URL discovery returned nothing while the web checks report content under a similar name.

usconnect llc.name: Bank account opening
usconnect llc.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers

report.headline: Onboard subject to a beneficial ownership certification with KYC and screening on the named owners and signer, review of the ten litigations and two liens, an operating address, and a Certificate of Good Standing from Delaware.

body.text: USCONNECT LLC is an LLC formed in Delaware, and the name suffix agrees with the entity type on the filing. A match was identified to the submitted business name, but the name exactly as submitted matches none of the filings or DBAs on the record, so the applied-for name and the filed name differ in some particular. The IRS holds a record for the submitted TIN and business name combination.

The record holds four Secretary of State filings: one is active, two are inactive, and the Delaware domestic filing carries no status or sub-status because Delaware publishes neither. The unpublished Delaware status is a limit of the registry and not a finding; it does mean good standing cannot be read off the record.
No phone number is on the record and no website was found from which to verify the business name, so the identification stage rests on the filings and the TIN alone.

gaps.point: Whether the Delaware domestic filing is in good standing, since Delaware publishes no filing status or sub-status.

body.text: The watchlist screen on the business returned one hit, which was reviewed and found not to be a valid match, so there is no sanctions or watchlist finding on the business. Adverse media screening returned no results.

The PEP screen returned no hits on submitted individuals or their relatives and close associates. No criminal history check is on the record for any person, and no people were submitted on the application, so the people side of the screening stage has not yet been run against named individuals.

gaps.point: Whether the owners and signer clear sanctions, PEP and criminal history screening, since no individuals have been named and screened.

body.text: The industry is classified as All Other Telecommunications, which is not a high-risk or prohibited industry under the classification applied. No website, third-party profile or other web activity is on the record, so there is no evidence of a second line of business beyond the classification, and nothing to test the classification against either.

The submitted office address matches the record, is deliverable and is a commercial property, but it is associated with a known registered agent, and the state of that address does not publish filing status. A registered-agent address is ordinary for a Delaware LLC; it is where the entity receives service, not where it operates, so the record does not establish where the business actually does business. No licence search is on the record for the industry or any jurisdiction.

gaps.point: Where the business actually operates, since the only address on the record is a registered agent's and no website or profile places it anywhere.

body.text: No people were submitted on the application and none were verified against the record, and no KYC decision is on file, so ownership and signing authority rest entirely on what the applicant will attest to. For a Delaware LLC the filing itself names no members or managers, so the record cannot supply the owners in their absence.

Seven related businesses were found connected to USCONNECT LLC. The record does not say whether any of them owns, is owned by, or shares management with the entity, so the complexity of the ownership structure cannot be read from the connections alone; no related-entity result is on the record.

gaps.point: Who owns 25% or more of USCONNECT LLC and who is authorised to sign, since no individuals were submitted or verified.
Whether any of the seven connected businesses sits in the ownership chain or shares control.
gaps.noAction: The connections are reviewed through the beneficial ownership certification: if a connected business is an owner it will be disclosed there, and a connection that is not disclosed is a fact for the file, not a step on its own.

body.text: Two liens are recorded against the business and ten litigations name it. The business has no bankruptcy filings. Ten actions is a substantial volume for a telecommunications LLC, and the record does not say which side the business is on, whether any carry a money judgment, or what the two liens secure and for whom, so none of them can yet be read as ordinary trade finance or as a creditor problem.
No PPP loan record is held. No people were submitted, so no liens, litigation or bankruptcies were searched against individuals; those searches follow once the owners are named.

gaps.point: Which side USCONNECT LLC is on in the ten litigations, their status, and whether any carries a money judgment.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A read of each litigation record for the party role, case status and judgment amount.

gaps.point: What the two liens secure, for which secured party, and whether either is open.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A read of each lien filing for the secured party, collateral description and filing status.

followUps.text:
Obtain the beneficial ownership certification and run KYC, sanctions, PEP and criminal history screening on each 25% owner and the account signer.
No people were submitted or verified, no KYC decision is on file, and the Delaware filing names no members.

Review the ten litigations for the business's party role, case status and any money judgment.
Ten actions name the business and the record does not say which side it is on or what was awarded.

Review the two liens for the secured party, the collateral and whether either is still open.
Two liens are recorded and the record does not say what they secure or whether they are satisfied.

Obtain an operating address and evidence of operations, such as a lease, utility bill or invoice.
The only address on the record is a registered agent's, and no website or profile places the business anywhere.

Submit an RFI for a Delaware Certificate of Good Standing.
Delaware publishes no filing status or sub-status, so good standing cannot be read from the record.

Confirm the legal name on the application against the active filing.
A match was identified, but the name exactly as submitted matches none of the filings or DBAs on the record.

kami agbeti.name: Bank account opening
kami agbeti.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to KYC on Kami Agbeti as sole proprietor, a stated line of work, and personal lien, litigation and bankruptcy searches; the record holds an IRS TIN match and clear business-level screenings but no filing, website or profile identifying the business beyond its owner.

body.text: KAMI AGBETI is submitted as a sole proprietorship and the entity type is verified as such. The business has no Secretary of State filings, and the submitted name matches no state filing or DBA on file, so the name and the office address cannot be matched to a registration. For a sole proprietorship trading under its owner's own name that is the expected shape of the record: no formation filing is required, and none exists to carry a status or sub-status.

The IRS holds a record for the submitted TIN and business name combination, which is the one independent source on the record tying the name to a taxpayer. No website was found, so no business name could be read from the web, and no filing or profile supplies a second account of the name.

gaps.point: Whether the Kami Agbeti on the application is the taxpayer the IRS record names, since no filing carries the name or the address and the TIN match is the only tie on the record.
Whether the business is in good standing with a Secretary of State.
gaps.noAction: A sole proprietorship has no Secretary of State registration to carry a status, so there is no standing to confirm.

body.text: Watchlist screening of the business returned no hits, politically exposed person screening of the submitted individuals and their relatives and close associates returned no hits, and no adverse media was found. Nothing on the record raises a sanctions or enforcement obligation for the business or the individual behind it.

The industry classification returned insufficient data, no website URL was found, and no third-party profiles were found, so the record carries no account of what the business does. Without a line of work no licensing requirement can be identified, and no license check is on the record to read against one.

The submitted office address is a residential property to which the USPS can deliver mail. It matches no state filing and the business is not registered in the state of the address, both of which follow from the business having no filings at all. A residential operating address is ordinary for a sole proprietorship.

gaps.point: What the business does and whether that activity is eligible under policy, since the classification returned insufficient data and no website or profile describes it.
Whether the activity requires a license where the business operates and whether one is held in the owner's name.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A license search keyed to the stated line of work and the jurisdiction of the submitted address.

body.text: The business is a sole proprietorship, so ownership and control sit with one individual and there is no structure to resolve: the owner is the business, the authorised signer, and the party any attestation describes. No related businesses were found, and nothing on the record points to another entity or a registered agent standing between the individual and the business.

The people check has no result on this record and no KYC decision is on file, so the individual behind the name has not been verified against any source here. For a business of this kind that verification is the whole of the ownership question.

gaps.point: Whether Kami Agbeti, as sole proprietor and signer, has been identified and verified, since no person verification or KYC decision is on the record.

body.text: No liens, litigation or bankruptcy filings were found against the business. A sole proprietorship has no legal existence apart from its owner, so the owner's personal liens, judgments and bankruptcies bear on the account as directly as the business's would; those searches are not on this record, and the clear business-level results speak only to the name as submitted.

gaps.point: Whether Kami Agbeti personally carries liens, litigation or bankruptcy filings, since the business has no separate legal person and only the business-level searches have run.

followUps.text:
Complete KYC on Kami Agbeti as sole proprietor and signer, with government ID and proof of the submitted address.
The business has no filing to match the name or address against; the IRS record for the TIN and name is the only tie on the record, and no person verification or KYC decision is on file.

Obtain the applicant's description of the business activity and expected account use, then run a license search against it.
The industry classification returned insufficient data and no website or third-party profile was found, so eligibility and licensing cannot be read from the record.

Order lien, litigation and bankruptcy searches on Kami Agbeti personally.
A sole proprietorship has no legal person apart from its owner, so the clear business-level results cover only the submitted name.

enclos tensile structures, inc..name: Bank account opening
enclos tensile structures, inc..brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to a beneficial ownership certification and control-person verification, disposition of the adverse media match, and review of the five litigations.

body.text: ENCLOS TENSILE STRUCTURES, INC. is a Minnesota corporation with an active domestic filing, and the submitted name matches that filing exactly; the name's suffix agrees with the entity type on the filing. The record holds 35 state filings for the business and every one of them is active, which is a footprint consistent with a contractor registered to work across many states. The IRS holds a record for the submitted TIN and business name together, so the tax identity is tied to this entity.

Minnesota does not publish a good-standing sub-status for the domestic filing, so standing beyond the active status is not on the record. The business's website carries a name similar to, rather than identical with, the submitted legal name, which is ordinary where a corporation trades under a shortened form of its registered name. No phone number was submitted, so none was verified.

gaps.point: Whether the Minnesota domestic filing is in good standing, since the state publishes an active status but no sub-status.

body.text: Watchlist screening on the business name returned one hit that was reviewed and found not to be a valid match, so no sanctions or enforcement obligation arises from the name. Politically exposed person screening returned no hits on the individuals screened or their relatives and close associates. Adverse media was found against the business; the subject and date of the coverage are not carried on the record, so what it concerns and whether it bears on the account is not yet established.

No people were submitted with the application, so no individual has been screened for sanctions, PEP status or criminal history in their own right. Those screens run once a control person is submitted.

gaps.point: What the adverse media coverage concerns and whether it names this business or a similarly named one.

body.text: The business is classified as an Other Foundation, Structure, and Building Exterior Contractor, which is not a high-risk or prohibited industry under a standard commercial banking policy. The submitted office address matches the record, the USPS delivers to it, and it is a commercial property; the business is active in the state of that address. A website was found and was online when the record was ordered, it shows the submitted office address, and third-party profiles for the business were found and are all online. Taken together the web presence is consistent with a contractor operating from the address given.

No licence check is on the record. Specialty contracting is licensed at state or local level in many of the jurisdictions where the business holds filings, so whether it is licensed where it performs work, and in whose name, is not established.

gaps.point: Whether the business holds the contractor licences required in the states where it performs work, and whether they are held by the entity or an individual.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A contractor licence search in the operating states, matched to the business and its officers.

body.text: No officer, owner or signer was submitted with the application, so no person has been verified against the filings and no KYC decision has been made. The entity is a corporation, so beneficial ownership is held through shares and is not visible on state filings; it has to come from the certification. Who controls the business and who is authorised to sign is therefore not established on the record as it stands.

The record links the business to 24 other businesses through 28 connections. For a corporation holding filings in many states, affiliated entities and shared officers are a plausible explanation, but whether any of those businesses is a parent, a sibling under common ownership or merely a neighbour at a shared address is not carried on the record.

gaps.point: Who the beneficial owners and the control person are, since no individual was submitted and the filings do not show shareholders.
Which of the 24 connected businesses share ownership or officers with the applicant, and whether any is a parent entity.

body.text: No UCC or tax liens were found against the business and it has no bankruptcy filings. For a contractor formed in 2022 the absence of equipment or working-capital financing on file is unremarkable. The business is named in five litigations; which side it is on and whether any carries a money judgment is not carried on the record. Construction disputes over payment and performance are ordinary for the trade, but five matters against a corporation of this age warrant reading before the account opens.
No people were submitted, so no lien, litigation or bankruptcy search has been run on an individual. Those searches run once a control person is submitted.

gaps.point: Whether the business is plaintiff or defendant in each of the five litigations, and whether any resulted in a money judgment.
Whether the control person carries liens, litigation or bankruptcy filings, since no person was submitted for search.

followUps.text:
Obtain the beneficial ownership certification and submit the control person for identity, screening and public-records checks.
No individual was submitted, so ownership, signing authority and the person-level screens are all open.

Review the adverse media match and record whether it concerns this business and what it alleges.
Adverse media was found but its subject is not on the record.

Pull the five litigation records and note the business's side in each and any money judgment.
Five matters are on file for a corporation formed in 2022 and none is characterised.

Submit an RFI for a Minnesota Certificate of Good Standing.
The domestic filing is active but Minnesota publishes no good-standing sub-status.

Confirm contractor licensing in the states where the business performs work, and in whose name the licences are held.
The trade is licensed in many jurisdictions and no licence check is on the record.

Identify which of the 24 connected businesses share ownership or officers with the applicant.
The connections are on the record but their nature is not, and a parent or affiliate changes who the account is really for.
