Progress is taking shape at the Cleveland Clinic Neurological Institute, where ETS is installing the project’s ETFE canopy systems.

Lightweight and highly transparent, ETFE helps create bright, open, weather-protected spaces while giving the canopies a distinctive architectural presence. As installation moves forward, we’re excited to see these systems become an increasingly visible part of the project.

A few highlights from the installation:
• 2 individual canopy structures
• 26 ETFE cushions/panels
• 130 tons of supporting steel

We’re excited to be working alongside an outstanding team to bring this project to life:
Cleveland Clinic 
Hopkins Architects 
Stantec 
Turner Construction Company
LeMessurier
Enclos Corp 

Great work by everyone involved as we continue making progress in Cleveland!

A stadium has to work long before kickoff, and long after the final whistle.

ETS designs and delivers lightweight roofs, canopies, and building envelopes for venues that transform for sports, concerts, and events while balancing long spans, daylight, weather protection, and architectural identity.

Explore our stadium expertise: https://ets-na.com/expertise/markets/stadiums/

The first ETFE roof cushion has been installed at the new Nissan Stadium!

After months of work on the cable net system, installing the ETFE cushions marks an exciting next phase for the roof. The first cushion spans approximately 12’-8” wide by 220’-0” long (2,785 square feet) and is one of 155 cushions that will ultimately form the stadium’s 341,283-square-foot transparent/translucent roof system.

Each lightweight ETFE cushion is composed of 2 layers of ETFE and is installed over 200 feet above the field, bringing the vision for the stadium roof one step closer to reality.

This milestone is the result of extensive planning and coordination across the project team, both on the ground and high above the field: Union Ironworkers Local 492 Nashville, Tn., ZDI Rope Access, Maxim Crane Works, LP, BrandSafway, icon Mechanical, and Tennessee Builders Alliance.

One cushion down, 154 to go!

Last month marked a major milestone at the New Nissan Stadium – the cable net was officially pinned!

Reaching this point represents months of planning, coordination, and precise execution by the teams working above the field and behind the scenes. With the cable net fully connected, another defining element of the stadium’s ETFE roof system has taken shape.

Thank you to our project partners Union Ironworkers Local 492 Nashville, Tn., ZDI Rope Access, VSL International Ltd., Maxim Crane Works, LP, Solid Platforms, INC, and Tennessee Builders Alliance for their continued collaboration on this landmark project.

Pictured: ETS team member Alex, nominated by the site crew, had the honor of placing the final pin. A fitting finish to a significant team effort!

Another milestone in the books as work continues overhead at New Nissan Stadium.

Another key milestone is underway at the new Nissan Stadium!

Following the successful pinning of the top net, crews installed the vertical posts that connect the upper and lower cable nets and help define the roof’s final form.

These photos offer a close-up look at the precision and expertise required for "hanging the wind chimes." Every pin installation represents careful planning, coordination, and execution by specialized crews working together to bring this complex roof structure to life.

Thank you to our project partners Union Ironworkers Local 492 Nashville, Tn., ZDI Rope Access, VSL International Ltd., Maxim Crane Works, LP, Solid Platforms, INC, and Tennessee Builders Alliance for their continued collaboration on this landmark project.

The vision for Nashville’s new stadium becomes more visible with every connection!

Pregame, but make it architectural.

As Atlanta hosts a semifinal match, the energy around the stadium will start long before kickoff.

ETS’ PTFE canopy structures at The Home Depot Backyard help support the outdoor gathering spaces that make major event days feel memorable, comfortable, and connected.

Along with nearby ETS work at the Georgia World Congress Center, these projects show how tensile architecture can shape the fan experience beyond the stadium bowl.

And for those flying out after the final whistle, ETS’ work may come back into view at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, where the ATL drop-off canopies feature a long-span pressurized ETFE cushion system and the largest ETFE cushion application in North America.

Match day is not just what happens on the field. It is everything that happens around it.

The deeper the tournament goes, the bigger the stage becomes!

As quarterfinal play brings Los Angeles Stadium back into the global spotlight, we are highlighting one of the most ambitious stadium roof structures ever built.

Known outside tournament play as SoFi Stadium, the venue features the world’s largest cable net roof structure: a 1.3 million-square-foot roof supported by an arching steel truss compression ring and covered with translucent ETFE.

The roof includes 302 ETFE panels, each approximately 60 feet by 60 feet, and 46 mechanized vents that help heat dissipate from the venue.

For ETS, the project began well before installation. Through a design-assist phase with the project consultants, ETS helped develop a technically and commercially viable roof and ETFE cladding system, supporting budget, schedule, logistics, and construction planning.

Learn more about the project at ets-na.com/projects/sofi-stadium

HKS Architects 
AECOM Hunt 
Turner Construction Company
Walter P Moore

A stadium can become part of a city’s identity.

Originally opened in 1983, BC Place was transformed from the world’s largest air-supported dome into a state-of-the-art venue with a cable-supported retractable roof.

ETS helped deliver that transformation by installing the new roof system’s fixed fabric panels: 36 outer panels and 36 inner panels, with the largest spanning 220 feet and covering approximately 10,000 square feet each.

The result is a lighter, brighter venue that redefined BC Place as a year-round, open-air stadium with 25,000 square feet of open sky from the interior.

As tournament play continues in Vancouver, BC Place remains a powerful example of tensile membrane design at civic scale.

Stantec 
schlaich bergermann partner

Stadiums are not just built for the game. Stadiums are built for arrival, movement, atmosphere, broadcast, and memory.

At Los Angeles Stadium, ETS’ work on the cable net roof structure is part of a venue designed to perform at a global scale while creating an unforgettable experience for fans.

As today’s match puts the stadium back in the spotlight, we are looking at the architectural systems that help make major sports venues feel iconic.

Explore lightweight stadium design at ets-na.com/expertise/markets/stadiums

It’s match day in Los Angeles! As the U.S. takes the field at Los Angeles Stadium, one of the world’s most recognizable sports venues is back in the global spotlight.

Known outside the World Cup as SoFi Stadium, this venue reflects the scale, coordination, and design ambition behind today’s major sports environments.

ETS’ work at the stadium is part of that larger experience, helping shape a venue designed for visibility, performance, and unforgettable public moments.

HKS Architects

solawave corp.name: Bank account opening
solawave corp.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to review of the two open liens and the adverse media hit, identification and screening of the beneficial owners with an explanation of the eight connected businesses, and a Delaware Certificate of Good Standing.

body.text: SOLAWAVE CORP is a Delaware corporation formed in March 2022. The submitted name matches a state filing, the Corp suffix agrees with the entity type on the filing, and the IRS holds a record for the submitted TIN and business name together. The website found for the business carries the submitted name, so the filed entity, the tax identity and the public-facing identity line up. No phone number was submitted, so none was checked.

Five Secretary of State filings were found. Delaware, the domestic state, publishes neither a filing status nor a sub-status, so standing in the home state cannot be read from the record; this is a property of the state, not of the business. Of the remaining filings, two are active and one is inactive, and the record does not identify which state the inactive registration is in or when it lapsed.

gaps.point: Whether the Delaware corporation is in good standing, which Delaware does not publish on the filing.
Which state the inactive registration belongs to, why it lapsed, and whether the business still operates there.

body.text: The business name returned no sanctions or watchlist hits, and the PEP screen returned no hits on submitted individuals or their relatives and close associates. Adverse media was found against the business; the record carries the hit but not its subject matter, so whether it concerns the business itself, a product, or a namesake is not established and the disposition is open. No individuals were submitted, so the people-level sanctions, PEP and criminal history screens have not run against any owner or signer.

gaps.point: What the adverse media hit concerns and whether it relates to this business.
Whether any beneficial owner or signer carries a sanctions, PEP or criminal history hit, as no individuals were submitted for screening.

body.text: The business is classified under All Other Miscellaneous Manufacturing, which is not a high-risk or prohibited industry under a standard bank policy. A website was found and was online when the record was ordered, and the third-party profiles found are all online. No license search ran for this business, and the record does not say what it manufactures, so whether the product category carries a licensing or regulatory requirement is not covered.

The submitted office address matches a state filing, is deliverable and is a commercial property, and the website displays the same address. It is also associated with a known registered agent, which is ordinary for a Delaware corporation but means the address establishes where the company is served rather than where it manufactures. Whether the address is a commercial mail receiving agency was not determined.

gaps.point: Whether the product manufactured requires a license or regulatory registration in the jurisdiction where it is made or sold.
gaps.wouldAnswer: A license search for the product category and operating state, once the product is known.

gaps.point: Where the business physically operates, since the only address on the record is a registered agent address.

body.text: No individuals were submitted with the application, so no officer, owner or signer has been identified or verified against the filing, and no KYC decision exists on the record. Ten connections link SOLAWAVE CORP to eight other businesses; the record does not say what the connections are or whether any of those businesses holds an interest in this one. For a corporation that is three years old, that many linked entities points to a structure that is more than a single operating company, and the ownership chain is not on the record.

gaps.point: Who the beneficial owners and authorized signers are, as none were submitted.
How the eight connected businesses relate to SOLAWAVE CORP and whether any is a parent, subsidiary or affiliate under common ownership.

body.text: Two open liens were found against the business. The record does not identify the secured party, the collateral or whether they are UCC or tax filings. For a manufacturing corporation formed in 2022, UCC filings over equipment or inventory would be ordinary financing; a tax lien or an all-assets filing would not be, and the two cannot be told apart until the filings are read. No litigation naming the business and no bankruptcy filings were found. No individuals were submitted, so lien, litigation and bankruptcy searches on the owners did not run, and PPP loan data was not pulled.

gaps.point: Who the secured parties on the two open liens are, what each secures, and whether either is a tax lien.

followUps.text:
Pull the two open lien filings and record the secured party, the collateral and the filing type for each.
The record shows two open liens against a three-year-old manufacturer without saying whether they are equipment financing or a tax lien.

Review the adverse media hit, confirm whether it concerns this business, and document the disposition.
Adverse media was found against the business name and the record does not carry what it relates to.

Collect the beneficial ownership certification and signer list, verify each person against the Delaware filing, and screen them for sanctions, PEP, adverse media and criminal history.
No individuals were submitted, so nobody on the file has been identified or screened.

Ask the applicant to describe how the eight connected businesses relate to SOLAWAVE CORP and name any parent, subsidiary or affiliate under common ownership.
Ten connections link the business to eight other entities and the ownership structure is not on the record.

Identify the state of the inactive foreign registration and confirm whether the business still operates there.
One of five filings is inactive and the record does not say which or why.

Submit an RFI for a Delaware Certificate of Good Standing.
Delaware publishes neither a status nor a sub-status on the domestic filing.

Obtain a description of the product manufactured and the operating address, with a lease or utility bill, and confirm whether the product category requires a license.
The only address on the record is a registered agent address and no license search ran for the industry.

miette, llc.name: Bank account opening
miette, llc.brief:
Run the four assessments attached to this assessment workflow. Make sure to keep the tone of the assessment in the mindset of a financial services compliance analyst that works at a bank like Mercury who is onboarding businesses to their bank. 

Make sure the prose is very concise and do not be overtly verbose. Only share what is relevant to the decision.

Write no recommendation prose at all. Do not summarise the assessments or repeat what they established; the reader has just read them. The recommendation section is the follow-ups and nothing else.

Each follow-up is one thing to do before the account opens, with only the facts that justify it behind it. Two lines, at most three: the instruction, then why. If nobody could act on it tomorrow, leave it out — a connected business that is plainly a neighbour is a fact for the assessment, not a step. Steps come from what the record leaves open and from what a registry does not publish: a missing good-standing sub-status is an RFI, not a shrug.�skill-kyb-identification:Is this a real, distinct, active entity, and is it the one on the application?

Always:
- Verify the submitted business name matches a state filing
- Verify the submitted address matches a state filing
- Identify Secretary of State filings (domestic and foreign)
- Identify Certificate of Good Standing or Secretary of State filings sub status is in good standing
- Identify unsubmitted entity classification type
- Identify unsubmitted industry classification 
- Identify unsubmitted web presence and third-party profiles
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers 
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

If submitted:
- Verify that the TIN belongs to a name associated with the business entity. If a TIN is not submitted do not elevate
- Verify DBA names, this is not a requirement, if the DBA is not submitted you literally dont have to mention it
- Verify entity classification type for the business entity
- Verify third-party profiles for the business entity
- Verify website presence for the business entity
- Verify email for the business entity
- Verify phone for the business entity�skill-kyb-3:Does the business, any UBO, or any signer trigger a sanctions or enforcement obligation?

Always:
- Flag hits for submitted business name Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted business name Adverse Media hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Sanctions / Watchlist hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people PEP hits
- Flag hits for submitted / found people Adverse Media hits�skill-kyb-activity:Is the industry eligible under policy, and is the business licensed where it operates?

Always:
- Identify whether the industry is a high-risk or prohibited industry
- Identify whether there is evidence of other industry activity not detected that point to high-risk or prohibited industries
- Identify presence and status of licenses required of the industry + jurisdiction. 
- Identify license link to officer / owner / person or business entity.�skill-1789767328449:Who ultimately owns this, who is authorized to sign, and does the attestation hold up?

Always:
- Identify unsubmitted officers or people associated
- Identify unsubmitted business entities listed as owners / officers
- Identify unsubmitted registered agents listed as owners / officers
- Identify complexity of ownership structure for the business entity

When submitted:
- Verify business entities listed as owners / officers
- Verify people listed as owners / officers
- Verify registered agents listed as owners / officers�skill-financial-standing:Does the business carry debts, judgments or insolvency that bear on the account?

Always:
- Identify UCC and tax liens on the business, open and closed, with the secured party and what is secured
- Identify litigation naming the business, which side it is on, and any money judgment
- Identify bankruptcy filings by the business
- Read each against the business's age and line of work: equipment finance and an SBA loan are ordinary for a bakery; a state tax lien or an all-assets blanket filing is not

When submitted:
- Identify liens, litigation and bankruptcies naming the submitted people

report.headline: Onboard subject to evidence that the inactive California filing has been revived, the detail of the four open liens, and identification and screening of the owners.

body.text: MIETTE, LLC is a California limited liability company formed in 2008. The submitted name matches the state filing, the LLC suffix agrees with the entity type on that filing, and no other registration carries the name, so the applicant and the registered entity are the same business.

The only Secretary of State filing is the California domestic registration, and it is inactive; the business holds no active filing in any state. California does not provide a sub-status, so the record does not say whether the filing is suspended, cancelled or dissolved, or whether it has since been revived. No TIN, DBA, phone or website was submitted, so none was verified.

gaps.point: Whether the inactive California filing has been revived, and what kind of inactive status it carries, is not on the record because the state does not publish a sub-status.

body.text: Sanctions and watchlist screening of the business name returned no hits. That is the only screening on the record: politically exposed person, adverse media and criminal history checks were not run, and no individuals have been identified for the business, so no person has been screened against any list.

gaps.point: Adverse media on the business and PEP screening of its owners and signers have not been run, so the screening stage covers the business name against watchlists and nothing else.

body.text: The submitted office address matches the state filing, the USPS delivers to it, and it is a commercial property. The business is registered in the state of that address, California, but its registration there is inactive, so the place of business and the state of formation agree while the entity's authority to operate in it does not.

No industry classification was run and no website or third-party profile was found or searched for, so the record does not say what the business does, whether that line of work is eligible under policy, or whether it requires a licence in California. No licence search is held for the business or any person.

gaps.point: The line of work is not on the record, so neither eligibility under the industry policy nor the licences it would require can be assessed.
No website or third-party profile is held for the business, so there is no independent account of its activity to read against the application.

body.text: No person is verified on the record: no officer, member or manager has been matched to the business, and no KYC decision is held. The entity is an LLC, so its members and managers are not derivable from the entity type and must come from the applicant's beneficial ownership certification and the state's filings. One related business is on the record through two connections; what it is and whether it shares ownership with MIETTE, LLC is not stated.

gaps.point: Who owns and controls the business is not established: no person has been identified or verified against the filing.
The related business on the record is not identified, so whether it is under common ownership or merely connected is open.

body.text: Four open liens are filed against the business. The record does not carry the secured parties, the filing dates or what is secured, so they cannot yet be read as ordinary equipment or working-capital finance or as a tax or blanket filing; on an entity whose only registration is inactive, that distinction decides the stage. No litigation names the business and it has no bankruptcy filings. No person-level search for liens, litigation or bankruptcies is held.

gaps.point: The secured party, filing date and collateral of each of the four open liens are not on the record, so their nature cannot be read against the business.

followUps.text:
Obtain a current California Certificate of Status or proof of revivor before opening the account.
The only filing is inactive and the state publishes no sub-status, so the record cannot say whether the entity is in standing.

Pull the four open liens and record the secured party, filing date and collateral of each.
The record counts them but does not say whether they are ordinary financing or tax or blanket filings.

Collect the beneficial ownership certification and verify each member and manager against the California filing, confirming whether the related business on the record is under common ownership.
No person is identified or verified on the record, and the connected business is not named.

Run PEP and adverse media screening on the business and on each owner and signer once identified.
Only the business name has been screened, and only against watchlists.

Establish the line of work from the applicant and run industry classification and a website search against it.
The record does not say what the business does, so eligibility and licensing cannot be assessed.
